texte.arena-amphitheater.info: Three storeys of arches, thirteen rings of stone seats and room for sixteen hundred on its own paved square. It has a gate for the living and a gate for the dead, and only one of them is ever busy both ways.
texte.arena-amphitheater.name: Great Amphitheatre
texte.arena-ausgang.info: The way out, with a bucket for the faint of stomach. It is emptied after every fight, and it is never empty.
texte.arena-ausgang.name: Arena Exit
texte.arena-eingang.info: The ticket hut, skull on the roof. Seats are numbered, limbs are not.
texte.arena-eingang.name: Arena Entrance
texte.arena-sand.info: A round sand pit with a stone ring and three rows of planks. Men walk in through the gate; how many walk out is up to the gods and the crowd.
texte.arena-sand.name: Arena
texte.arena-sandgrube-viertel.info: The first arena, now with neighbours: a ring of planks in a rectangle of sheds, patched tents and puddles. Nobody knows who lives in them, and nobody has ever come out to complain about the noise.
texte.arena-sandgrube-viertel.name: Sand Pit
texte.arena-sandgrube.info: The first arena: a ring of planks around a pit of sand on its own square plot, a lanista's box and two sails for the nobility. Three to a seat, one way in, two ways out.
texte.arena-sandgrube.name: Sand Pit
texte.armoury.info: Every blade counted, every lock bronze. The count is always one short.
texte.armoury.name: Armoury
texte.bacchant-ranke-a.info: An empty amphora lies in the weeds. The worshippers drank the wine and then the evidence.
texte.bacchant-ranke-a.name: Bacchant Vine (amphora)
texte.bacchant-ranke-b.info: A small stone altar, stained purple, with a bronze cup. The god of excess accepts any offering, as long as it is too much.
texte.bacchant-ranke-b.name: Bacchant Vine (altar)
texte.bacchant-ranke.info: A wild tangle of vines with near-black berries and a torn ivy wreath. Eat one and dance, eat three and dance forever.
texte.bacchant-ranke.name: Bacchant Vine
texte.barracks.info: Bunks for twenty, smell for forty. The tally by the door is not for days served.
texte.barracks.name: Barracks
texte.baum-akazie-a.info: Someone hung a bronze helmet on this acacia and never came back for it. Shade for one, ventilation included.
texte.baum-akazie-a.name: Acacia, Helmet Hook
texte.baum-akazie-b.info: An acacia with a few bleached bones at its foot. Lunch was had here once, just not by the traveller.
texte.baum-akazie-b.name: Acacia, Picnic Leftovers
texte.baum-akazie-c.info: A parched acacia with rust-brown leaves, a frayed rope stub and three red rags. The local tourist board calls it a landmark.
texte.baum-akazie-c.name: Acacia, Dry Season
texte.baum-akazie.info: A flat-topped acacia, the only shade for a day in any direction. Lions, vultures and travellers all agree on that, and they rarely agree on anything else.
texte.baum-akazie.name: Acacia
texte.baum-apfel-a.info: Ripe apples above, rotting apples below. The tree knows the arena crowd will throw either.
texte.baum-apfel-a.name: Apple Tree, Windfall
texte.baum-apfel-b.info: A dented helmet makes a fine fruit basket. The previous owner no longer needs it to keep anything in.
texte.baum-apfel-b.name: Apple Tree, Helmet Basket
texte.baum-apfel-c.info: An old, half-bare apple tree with a board nailed to it, tallying something. Nobody admits what, and the bones nearby are not talking.
texte.baum-apfel-c.name: Apple Tree, Tally Board
texte.baum-apfel.info: Red apples, free for the taking. The worms were here first and they are not sharing.
texte.baum-apfel.name: Apple Tree
texte.baum-baobab-a.info: A baobab wrapped in iron chain with a padlock. Either the tree is valuable or something inside it is not allowed out.
texte.baum-baobab-a.name: Baobab, Chained
texte.baum-baobab-b.info: Rows of tally marks carved into the bark and old bones at the roots. The baobab keeps score better than the referee.
texte.baum-baobab-b.name: Baobab, Scoreboard
texte.baum-baobab-c.info: A leafless baobab with a shut plank door and a frayed rope stub. The door is locked from the outside, which says a lot.
texte.baum-baobab-c.name: Baobab, Dry Season
texte.baum-baobab.info: A baobab with a trunk like a wine jar. Hollow inside, which the locals use for storing water, grain and the occasional tax collector.
texte.baum-baobab.name: Baobab
texte.baum-birke-a.info: A birch with fresh tally marks among its natural black ones. Some recruit is counting the days, or the rods.
texte.baum-birke-a.name: Birch, Counted
texte.baum-birke-b.info: A birch with an arrow stuck in its trunk. It was not the target; the target ran.
texte.baum-birke-b.name: Birch, Target Practice
texte.baum-birke-c.info: A birch with a broken crown and yellowing leaves. It lost a fight with the wind and, judging by the bone, so did someone else.
texte.baum-birke-c.name: Birch, Snapped
texte.baum-birke.info: A pale birch. Its rods are flexible, cheap and well remembered by every recruit.
texte.baum-birke.name: Birch
texte.baum-buche-a.info: A carved heart, crossed out in red. Love is short, beech bark is patient.
texte.baum-buche-a.name: Beech, Crossed Heart
texte.baum-buche-b.info: A sword driven into the trunk, a little blood below. Whoever pulls it out becomes king, or at least the next to bleed.
texte.baum-buche-b.name: Beech, Stuck Sword
texte.baum-buche-c.info: A copper-leaved beech in autumn, with tally marks and a red stain at its foot. The leaves are not the only thing that fell here.
texte.baum-buche-c.name: Beech, Autumn Copper
texte.baum-buche.info: A broad beech with a smooth grey trunk. Burns long and hot, which the smith appreciates more than the beech does.
texte.baum-buche.name: Beech
texte.baum-dattelpalme-a.info: A date palm with a round bronze shield nailed to it. Excellent cover, as long as the enemy stands exactly there.
texte.baum-dattelpalme-a.name: Date Palm, Shield Nail
texte.baum-dattelpalme-b.info: A leaning date palm hung with dead brown fronds. Fashionable among palms, flammable among everyone.
texte.baum-dattelpalme-b.name: Date Palm, Withered Skirt
texte.baum-dattelpalme-c.info: Notches cut for climbing, red dates at the top and a stain at the bottom. The last notch was one too many.
texte.baum-dattelpalme-c.name: Date Palm, Climbing Notches
texte.baum-dattelpalme.info: A tall palm heavy with dates. Sweet enough for a senator, and the climb is steep enough to cull the greedy.
texte.baum-dattelpalme.name: Date Palm
texte.baum-eiche-skizze-a.info: A bronze helmet on one branch, a sword in the trunk. The oak collects armour the way other trees collect moss.
texte.baum-eiche-skizze-a.name: Old Oak, Trophy Branch
texte.baum-eiche-skizze-b.info: A hollow oak with bones tucked inside. Hide-and-seek champion, posthumously.
texte.baum-eiche-skizze-b.name: Old Oak, Hollow
texte.baum-eiche-skizze-c.info: Half dead after a lightning strike, charred down the middle, a frayed rope still tied to a bare limb. The gods aimed at the rope.
texte.baum-eiche-skizze-c.name: Old Oak, Lightning Struck
texte.baum-eiche-skizze.info: An oak older than the empire and twice as honest. Its roots have drunk from more battlefields than any legionary. Excellent shade, terrible witness.
texte.baum-eiche-skizze.name: Old Oak
texte.baum-farn-a.info: A tree fern with a broken spear shaft caught in its fronds. The fern survived the dinosaurs; this spear did not survive the fern.
texte.baum-farn-a.name: Tree Fern, Broken Spear
texte.baum-farn-b.info: A tree fern going brown at the edges. Too much sun, too little rain, and far too much arena runoff.
texte.baum-farn-b.name: Tree Fern, Wilting
texte.baum-farn-c.info: A short gladius rusting among the roots, with a little blood on the soil. Someone dropped it, and then everything else.
texte.baum-farn-c.name: Tree Fern, Lost Blade
texte.baum-farn.info: A fern grown tall enough to call itself a tree. It was old when the gods were young and has not been impressed since.
texte.baum-farn.name: Tree Fern
texte.baum-kokospalme.info: A leaning palm with a crown of coconuts. Every year it drops one on somebody, and every year the priests call it a sign.
texte.baum-kokospalme.name: Coconut Palm
texte.baum-lianen.info: A jungle tree hung with lianas. Good for swinging, better for hanging, and nobody here ever bothers to tell the two apart.
texte.baum-lianen.name: Liana Tree
texte.baum-mangrove.info: A mangrove standing on its roots in the brine. The crabs live underneath, the mosquitoes above, and lost sandals in between.
texte.baum-mangrove.name: Mangrove
texte.baum-olive.info: A gnarled olive tree, older than the oldest grudge in town. Oil for the lamps, oil for the wounds, oil for the bribes.
texte.baum-olive.name: Olive Tree
texte.baum-pappel.info: A tall, thin poplar. Soft wood, fast growth and no character at all, rather like a senator.
texte.baum-pappel.name: Poplar
texte.baum-tanne.info: A dark fir, straight as a spear. Makes good beams, good masts and, if business is slow, good coffins.
texte.baum-tanne.name: Fir
texte.baum-zypresse.info: A slim dark cypress, the traditional tree of graveyards. It grows near the arena for the same reason.
texte.baum-zypresse.name: Cypress
texte.beastrium.info: Three cages, all empty for now. The straw remembers what lived here, and so do the bones.
texte.beastrium.name: Beastrium
texte.bett-stroh.info: A wooden frame, old straw and one blanket. The fleas were here first and they pay no rent either.
texte.bett-stroh.name: Straw Bed
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i-a.info: Moss creeps along the shingle edges. In ten years it will own the house; it already pays more tax.
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i-a.name: Shingle Right A
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i-b.info: Patched with old shingles from a burnt barn. Nobody asked the barn.
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i-b.name: Shingle Right B
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i-c.info: A field stone weighs the shingles down against the storms. Sometimes against a lid.
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i-c.name: Shingle Right C
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i.info: Split wooden shingles, grey with age and green with moss. Light, cheap and as loyal as a hired guard.
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-i.name: Shingled Roof Slope, Right

texte.bk-block-dach-ab-j-d.name: Shingle Front D
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-j-e.info: A carpet of moss on the shingles. It holds the roof together better than the nails do.
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-j-e.name: Shingle Front E
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-j-f.info: An old axe sits in the roof since the inheritance was settled. Nobody dared to pull it out.
texte.bk-block-dach-ab-j-f.name: Shingle Front F

texte.bk-block-fenster-a.info: One shutter hangs crooked on a single hinge. It bangs all night, which helps nobody sleep.
texte.bk-block-fenster-a.name: Log Window A
texte.bk-block-fenster-b.info: Boarded shut with a cross plank. Either the family left, or the family is hiding.
texte.bk-block-fenster-b.name: Log Window B
texte.bk-block-fenster-d.info: An arrow in the shutter and a dark streak below. The hunting season had a slow start.
texte.bk-block-fenster-d.name: Log Window D
texte.bk-block-fenster.info: A small window with heavy shutters. Small, because glass is dear and neighbours are curious.
texte.bk-block-fenster.name: Log Window
texte.bk-block-giebel-a.info: A smoke hole under the roof. The smoke rarely finds it.
texte.bk-block-giebel-a.name: Log Gable A
texte.bk-block-giebel-ab.info: Top of a log gable, the other way round. The axe was no sharper.
texte.bk-block-giebel-ab.name: Log Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-block-giebel-auf.info: Top of a log gable, cut to the slope of the roof with a dull axe.
texte.bk-block-giebel-auf.name: Log Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-block-giebel-b.info: Carved notches against bad luck. Bad luck cannot read.
texte.bk-block-giebel-b.name: Log Gable B
texte.bk-block-giebel-c.info: A skull nailed under the roof. Officially to scare off spirits, unofficially a former tax collector.
texte.bk-block-giebel-c.name: Log Gable C
texte.bk-block-giebel.info: The gable is stacked from shorter logs. Every winter it creaks a little more like an old man.
texte.bk-block-giebel.name: Log Gable
texte.bk-block-tuer-a.info: An axe is stuck in the door frame. It was a discussion about firewood. The firewood won.
texte.bk-block-tuer-a.name: Log Door A
texte.bk-block-tuer.info: Planks, iron bands and a row of chalk marks. Each mark is a debt; each debt has a name.
texte.bk-block-tuer.name: Log Door
texte.bk-block-wand-a.info: One log was replaced. The old one went into the stove during the long winter, together with the chair.
texte.bk-block-wand-a.name: Log Wall A
texte.bk-block-wand-b.info: Moss grows in the chinks and a log has split. The owner calls it ventilation.
texte.bk-block-wand-b.name: Log Wall B

texte.bk-block-wand-d.name: Log Wall D

texte.bk-block-wand-oben.info: Upper storey of stacked logs. Warm, solid and very easy to set on fire.
texte.bk-block-wand-oben.name: Log Upper Wall
texte.bk-block-wand.info: Round logs on a fieldstone footing, moss in the gaps. Keeps out wolves, debt collectors and most of the winter.
texte.bk-block-wand.name: Log Wall

texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster-a.info: Boarded up from inside, the days scratched below. Somebody stopped counting.
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster-a.name: Half-Timbered Window A
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster-b.info: Same mat, newer braces. The carpenter was paid in turnips and built accordingly.
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster-b.name: Half-Timbered Window B
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster-d.info: The shutter hangs by one hinge and the scratches below go the wrong way. Nobody asks.
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster-d.name: Half-Timbered Window D
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster.info: A small window with a straw mat. Glass is for temples and fools.
texte.bk-fachwerk-fenster.name: Half-Timbered Window
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-a.info: Oak rails and cracked whitewash under the roof. Cheaper to patch than to admit the house is old.
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-a.name: Half-Timbered Gable A
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-ab.info: The other half of the oak gable. It sags towards the neighbour out of spite.
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-ab.name: Half-Timbered Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-auf.info: The pointed end of an oak gable. Woodpeckers keep trying it.
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-auf.name: Half-Timbered Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-b.info: Oak rails and cracked whitewash under the roof. Cheaper to patch than to admit the house is old.
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-b.name: Half-Timbered Gable B
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-c.info: Oak rails and cracked whitewash under the roof. Cheaper to patch than to admit the house is old.
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel-c.name: Half-Timbered Gable C
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel.info: Dark oak boards under the shingles. The owls hold the lease.
texte.bk-fachwerk-giebel.name: Half-Timbered Gable
texte.bk-fachwerk-tuer.info: A heavy oak door with iron straps. Built to keep out wolves, tax men and the in-laws, in that order.
texte.bk-fachwerk-tuer.name: Half-Timbered Door
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-a.info: The plaster came off and the wattle shows. Nobody fixes it; it is the only window that never needs cleaning.
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-a.name: Half-Timbered Wall A
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-b.info: A crack runs from beam to beam. Below it someone counts the days in scratches. Or the debts.
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-b.name: Half-Timbered Wall B
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-d.info: Two chains on two nails, one of them still sticky. The landlord calls it a reminder.
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-d.name: Half-Timbered Wall D
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-oben-a.info: A hook and a coil of rope, high up where the bailiff can see it. Subtle, as forest towns go.
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-oben-a.name: Half-Timbered Upper Wall A
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-oben.info: An upper floor of oak crosses and whitewash. Leans over the lane so the neighbours can share the rain.
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand-oben.name: Half-Timbered Upper Wall
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand.info: Oak beams and whitewash over wattle. The beams are the only honest part of the house.
texte.bk-fachwerk-wand.name: Half-Timbered Wall
texte.bk-feld.info: Furrows of dark earth with green shoots. Somebody sweated here so somebody else can eat in the stands.
texte.bk-feld.name: Ploughed Field
texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-a.info: Yellow lichen on wet slates. It grows faster than the fishermen's savings.
texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-a.name: Slate Right A
texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-b.info: Slates of three different quarries. The roofer calls it a pattern, the owner calls it robbery.
texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-b.name: Slate Right B

texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-c.name: Slate Right C
texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-d.info: A hole in the slates with a broken oar stuck through it. The roofer drowned before he finished.

texte.bk-kueste-dach-ab-i-e.info: Gull droppings, layered like a chronicle. Each storm washes a chapter away.

texte.bk-kueste-dach-flach.info: Blue-grey slates from the cliffs, quarried by men who are now at the bottom of them.
texte.bk-kueste-dach-flach.name: Slate Flat
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-a.info: Boarded up crosswise since the last storm. Or since the last visit from the harbour master.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-a.name: Fishhouse Window A
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-b.info: A net slung under the sill and gull droppings down the boards. The gulls pay no rent either.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-b.name: Fishhouse Window B
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-d.info: One shutter gone to the storm, a noose of net rope by the frame. Nobody in the house admits to tying it.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-d.name: Fishhouse Window D
texte.bk-kueste-fenster.info: A small window with sea-blue shutters, paint flaking in the salt wind. Glass is for rich people.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster.name: Fishhouse Window
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab.info: The falling verge, slate on tarred boards. Gulls sit here and judge the passers-by.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf.info: The rising verge, finished with a row of slates. The wind still finds its way in.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-kueste-giebel.info: Gable boards nailed over the attic where the nets and the drowned man's savings are kept.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel.name: Fishhouse Gable
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-a.info: A coil of rope on a nail and an oar by the door. Ready to row out, or to beat the debt collector.
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-a.name: Fishhouse Door A
texte.bk-kueste-tuer.info: A plank door in a stone frame, swollen shut every spring. Knock twice, then shout over the gulls.
texte.bk-kueste-tuer.name: Fishhouse Door
texte.bk-kueste-wand-a.info: A torn net hung out to dry, corks and all. It has been drying since the owner went out and did not come back.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-a.name: Fishhouse Wall A
texte.bk-kueste-wand-b.info: A tar patch, a crust of salt and a spare oar. Every storm takes a board, every winter a fisherman.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-b.name: Fishhouse Wall B
texte.bk-kueste-wand-d.info: Chalk tallies and a rusty anchor. One mark for every husband the sea kept; the widow stopped at thirteen.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-d.name: Fishhouse Wall D
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-a.info: A rope coil on a hook. In a fishing town everything is rope, and every rope has been a noose once.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-a.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall A
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-b.info: A square of tar slapped over rotten boards. It holds until the next gale, then it holds the gale.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-b.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall B
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-d.info: Chalk strokes for the catches and red crosses for the boats that stayed out. The crosses are winning.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-d.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall D
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben.info: Weatherboards on the upper floor, silver where the wind has scoured them. Leaks only when it rains sideways.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall
texte.bk-kueste-wand.info: Tarred weatherboards on a fieldstone footing. Smells of fish, salt and whatever the tide left in the cellar.
texte.bk-kueste-wand.name: Fishhouse Wall
texte.bk-lehm-boden.info: Stamped clay with straw in it. Spill something and it becomes part of the floor.
texte.bk-lehm-boden.name: Mud-and-Timber Floor
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-i.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-i.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Right
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-a.info: Same straw, a hole the size of a fist. Something small is already moving in.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-a.name: Thatch Front A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-b.info: Same straw, a little more rot on the north side. Nobody has noticed. Nobody looks up.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-b.name: Thatch Front B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-c.info: Same straw, wearing its moss like a bad toupee.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-c.name: Thatch Front C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-d.info: The roof gave way here. The crow took the opportunity and has not left since.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-d.name: Thatch Front D
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-e.info: Stripped to the laths. Someone ate the thatch. Someone else ate that someone.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-e.name: Thatch Front E
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-f.info: Blood runs down the straw. The roofer fell, the roof held. Priorities.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-f.name: Thatch Front F
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k-a.info: The ridge. Straw sticks up like a cheap wig; the wind has opinions about it. Patched twice, trusted never.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k-a.name: Thatch Front Ridge A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k-b.info: The ridge. Straw sticks up like a cheap wig; the wind has opinions about it. Longer on one end, as if cut by a drunk.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k-b.name: Thatch Front Ridge B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k-c.info: The ridge. Straw sticks up like a cheap wig; the wind has opinions about it. Furry with moss.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k-c.name: Thatch Front Ridge C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k.info: The ridge. Straw sticks up like a cheap wig; the wind has opinions about it.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-k.name: Thatch Front Ridge
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn-a.info: The ridge falls apart at the left end. So does the roofer's excuse. Patched twice, trusted never.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn-a.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable L A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn-b.info: The ridge falls apart at the left end. So does the roofer's excuse. Longer on one end, as if cut by a drunk.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn-b.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable L B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn-c.info: The ridge falls apart at the left end. So does the roofer's excuse. Furry with moss.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn-c.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable L C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn.info: The ridge falls apart at the left end. So does the roofer's excuse.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-kn.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable L
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks-a.info: Where ridge and gable meet, the straw gave up on straight lines. Patched twice, trusted never.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks-a.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable R A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks-b.info: Where ridge and gable meet, the straw gave up on straight lines. Longer on one end, as if cut by a drunk.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks-b.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable R B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks-c.info: Where ridge and gable meet, the straw gave up on straight lines. Furry with moss.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks-c.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable R C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks.info: Where ridge and gable meet, the straw gave up on straight lines.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-ks.name: Thatch Front Ridge+Gable R
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n-a.info: The left end of the thatch. It slumps over the boards like a drunk over a bar. Patched twice, trusted never.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n-a.name: Thatch Front Gable L A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n-b.info: The left end of the thatch. It slumps over the boards like a drunk over a bar. Longer on one end, as if cut by a drunk.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n-b.name: Thatch Front Gable L B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n-c.info: The left end of the thatch. It slumps over the boards like a drunk over a bar. Furry with moss.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n-c.name: Thatch Front Gable L C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n.info: The left end of the thatch. It slumps over the boards like a drunk over a bar.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-n.name: Thatch Front Gable L
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r-a.info: A ragged eave. It sheds rain, mostly onto whoever stands under it.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r-a.name: Thatch Front Eave A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r-b.info: A crooked eave, one handspan too short. The roofer ran out of straw and patience.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r-b.name: Thatch Front Eave B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r-c.info: A mossy eave, sagging at the corner like a bad decision.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r-c.name: Thatch Front Eave C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r.info: The edge of the thatch, frayed and uneven. The roofer was paid by the day, not by the metre.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-r.name: Thatch Front Eave
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn-a.info: Thatch on the left corner, in free fall for decades but never quite landed. Patched twice, trusted never.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn-a.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable L A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn-b.info: Thatch on the left corner, in free fall for decades but never quite landed. Longer on one end, as if cut by a drunk.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn-b.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable L B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn-c.info: Thatch on the left corner, in free fall for decades but never quite landed. Furry with moss.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn-c.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable L C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn.info: Thatch on the left corner, in free fall for decades but never quite landed.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rn.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable L
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs-a.info: Where eave and side meet, the thatch gives up completely. The corner is held up by habit and a bit of rope. Patched twice, trusted never.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs-a.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable R A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs-b.info: Where eave and side meet, the thatch gives up completely. The corner is held up by habit and a bit of rope. Longer on one end, as if cut by a drunk.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs-b.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable R B
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs-c.info: Where eave and side meet, the thatch gives up completely. The corner is held up by habit and a bit of rope. Furry with moss.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs-c.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable R C
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs.info: Where eave and side meet, the thatch gives up completely. The corner is held up by habit and a bit of rope.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-rs.name: Thatch Front Eave+Gable R
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-s-a.info: The side of the thatch, hanging out over the gable boards. Nobody trimmed it. Nobody wanted to climb up.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-s-a.name: Thatch Front Gable R A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-s-b.info: The side of the thatch, hanging out over the gable boards. Nobody trimmed it. Nobody wanted to climb up.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-s-b.name: Thatch Front Gable R B

texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j-s.name: Thatch Front Gable R
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Front
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-i.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-i.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Left
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j-a.info: Weathered straw bundles, tied and patched. The mice still refuse to pay rent.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j-a.name: Thatch Rear A
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j-b.info: Weathered straw bundles, tied and patched. The mice still refuse to pay rent.

texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Rear
texte.bk-lehm-dach-flach.info: A flat bed of thatch. Good for drying fish and hiding from tax men.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-flach.name: Thatched Roof, Flat
texte.bk-lehm-fenster-a.info: Boarded up from inside. Someone counted the days on the wall below. Then they stopped counting.
texte.bk-lehm-fenster-a.name: Mud-and-Timber Window A
texte.bk-lehm-fenster-b.info: Dried fish on a string, and a rat nobody admits to. Dinner hangs where everyone can see it.
texte.bk-lehm-fenster-b.name: Mud-and-Timber Window B
texte.bk-lehm-fenster-d.info: The shutter hangs by one hinge and the scratches below go the wrong way. Nobody asks who wanted out.
texte.bk-lehm-fenster-d.name: Mud-and-Timber Window D
texte.bk-lehm-fenster.info: A hole in the wall with a straw mat for a curtain. Keeps out the light, lets in the flies.
texte.bk-lehm-fenster.name: Mud-and-Timber Window
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-a.info: Cracked clay between old timber rails. The repair is cheaper than admitting the roof is falling.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-a.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable A
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-ab.info: The other half of the timber gable. Nobody remembers which half was built first.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-ab.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-auf.info: The pointed end of a timber gable. The birds nest here and pay no rent.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-auf.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-b.info: Cracked clay between old timber rails. The repair is cheaper than admitting the roof is falling.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-b.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable B
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-c.info: Cracked clay between old timber rails. The repair is cheaper than admitting the roof is falling.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-c.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable C
texte.bk-lehm-giebel.info: Boards nailed up under the end of the roof. They hold, mostly.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable
texte.bk-lehm-rang.info: Rows of plank benches. Splinters are free and so is the view of the killing.
texte.bk-lehm-rang.name: Mud-and-Timber Tiers
texte.bk-lehm-schild.info: A crooked board on a stick with a daub of paint. Nobody can read, so a picture of a sausage does the job.
texte.bk-lehm-schild.name: Mud-and-Timber Sign
texte.bk-lehm-tuer.info: A plank door that sticks in summer and in winter. In spring it merely creaks.
texte.bk-lehm-tuer.name: Mud-and-Timber Door
texte.bk-lehm-wand-a.info: A fresh daub of clay over last winter's hole. Still damp, still lumpy, still cheaper than a mason.
texte.bk-lehm-wand-a.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall A
texte.bk-lehm-wand-b.info: A crack wide enough to post letters through. The straw inside is the only thing holding it together.
texte.bk-lehm-wand-b.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall B
texte.bk-lehm-wand-d.info: A rat nailed up by its tail. Pest control, warning and decoration in one.
texte.bk-lehm-wand-d.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall D
texte.bk-lehm-wand-oben-a.info: A bird nests under the beam and pays its rent on the wall below.
texte.bk-lehm-wand-oben-a.name: Mud-and-Timber Upper Wall A
texte.bk-lehm-wand-oben.info: An upper floor of clay on a crooked frame. The brace is the only straight thing in the house.
texte.bk-lehm-wand-oben.name: Mud-and-Timber Upper Wall
texte.bk-lehm-wand.info: Clay packed over a timber frame. Cracks come free of charge, draughts are included.
texte.bk-lehm-wand.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall
texte.bk-marmor-boden.info: Marble slabs with a purple inlay. Slippery when wet, and it is always wet with something.
texte.bk-marmor-boden.name: Marble Floor
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i-a.info: Pigeons have discovered marble. It is the only luxury they share with the owner.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i-a.name: Marble Slab Right A
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i-d.info: A cracked slab. Marble is hard, but a falling tenant is harder.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i-d.name: Marble Slab Right D
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Right
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j-a.info: Pigeons have discovered marble. It is the only luxury they share with the owner.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j-a.name: Marble Slab Front A
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j-d.info: A cracked slab. Marble is hard, but a falling tenant is harder.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j-d.name: Marble Slab Front D
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Front

texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-i-d.name: Marble Slab Left D

texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j-a.name: Marble Slab Rear A
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j-d.info: A cracked slab. Marble is hard, but a falling tenant is harder.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j-d.name: Marble Slab Rear D
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Rear
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach-a.info: Pigeons have discovered marble. It is the only luxury they share with the owner.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach-a.name: Marble Slab Flat A
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach-d.info: A cracked slab. Marble is hard, but a falling tenant is harder.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach-d.name: Marble Slab Flat D
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach.info: Flat marble slabs on top. Ideal for a terrace and for looking down on the street.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach.name: Marble-Slab Roof, Flat
texte.bk-marmor-fenster.info: A tall window with a bronze grille and a little gilded pediment. Bars, but tasteful ones.
texte.bk-marmor-fenster.name: Marble Window
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-ab.info: The other gilded pediment edge. Symmetry costs extra and the owner paid.
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-ab.name: Marble Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-auf.info: A gilded pediment edge. The gods look down from here, the owner looks down on everyone else.
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-auf.name: Marble Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-marmor-giebel.info: A marble gable, straight as a senator claims to be.
texte.bk-marmor-giebel.name: Marble Gable
texte.bk-marmor-rang.info: White marble tiers for people who never sit on anything cheaper. The blood looks better from here.
texte.bk-marmor-rang.name: Marble Tiers
texte.bk-marmor-schild.info: A bronze plaque on a marble pedestal. Whatever it advertises, you cannot afford it.
texte.bk-marmor-schild.name: Marble Sign
texte.bk-marmor-tuer.info: A bronze door with gilded studs. Heavy enough to keep out the mob and, on a good day, the creditors.
texte.bk-marmor-tuer.name: Marble Door
texte.bk-marmor-wand-a.info: A crack filled with gilded putty. Patched like the reputation of the man who paid for it.
texte.bk-marmor-wand-a.name: Marble Wall A
texte.bk-marmor-wand-b.info: A donor's inscription, half chiselled away. He fell from favour; the wall only fell halfway.
texte.bk-marmor-wand-b.name: Marble Wall B
texte.bk-marmor-wand-d.info: Something red runs down from the gilded band. The owner insists it is wine. It is always wine.
texte.bk-marmor-wand-d.name: Marble Wall D
texte.bk-marmor-wand-oben.info: An upper floor of polished marble. Up here the screams from the street arrive slightly muffled.
texte.bk-marmor-wand-oben.name: Marble Upper Wall

texte.bk-palm-fenster-a.info: Something drying in the window. It will never dry. Nothing here ever dries.
texte.bk-palm-fenster-a.name: Stilt Bamboo Window A
texte.bk-palm-fenster-b.info: A broken shutter, eaten by beetles. The beetles were eaten by the family.
texte.bk-palm-fenster-b.name: Stilt Bamboo Window B
texte.bk-palm-fenster-d.info: Hanging shutter, tally marks of a moneylender below. He reads them by torchlight from the boat.
texte.bk-palm-fenster-d.name: Stilt Bamboo Window D
texte.bk-palm-fenster.info: A slot in the bamboo, for air. The air here is mostly wet.
texte.bk-palm-fenster.name: Stilt Bamboo Window
texte.bk-palm-giebel-a.info: Gable poles, dark with rain and smoke. Something grows on them that has no name yet.
texte.bk-palm-giebel-a.name: Stilt Bamboo Gable A

texte.bk-palm-tuer.info: A door on stilts. The ladder is pulled up at night, along with any trust.
texte.bk-palm-tuer.name: Stilt Bamboo Door
texte.bk-palm-wand-a.info: New poles beside old ones. The old ones are mostly mould now, holding hands with the new.
texte.bk-palm-wand-a.name: Stilt Bamboo Wall A
texte.bk-palm-wand-b.info: A split pole. Rain comes in sideways, gossip goes out the same way.
texte.bk-palm-wand-b.name: Stilt Bamboo Wall B
texte.bk-palm-wand-d.info: A small skull hung on a vine. Visitors are reminded to pay before they leave.
texte.bk-palm-wand-d.name: Stilt Bamboo Wall D
texte.bk-palm-wand-oben-a.info: A nest under the beam. Whatever lives in it is smarter than the landlord.
texte.bk-palm-wand-oben-a.name: Stilt Bamboo Upper Wall A
texte.bk-palm-wand-oben.info: Upper bamboo wall under the palm eaves. Green with moss, proud of it.
texte.bk-palm-wand-oben.name: Stilt Bamboo Upper Wall
texte.bk-palm-wand.info: Bamboo poles lashed with vine, on stilts above the mud. Below lives the damp; above lives the debt.
texte.bk-palm-wand.name: Stilt Bamboo Wall
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster-a.info: A clay pot on the sill and a net on a line. Breakfast, laundry and evidence, all in one window.
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster-a.name: Stilt Plank Window A
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster-b.info: Shuttered tight against the mosquitoes, which have long since moved in.
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster-b.name: Stilt Plank Window B
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster-d.info: A red cross painted on the shutter. Fever inside. The neighbours row a little faster past this one.
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster-d.name: Stilt Plank Window D
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster.info: A shutter propped open on a stick. Kick the stick and the conversation is over.
texte.bk-pfahl-fenster.name: Stilt Plank Window
texte.bk-pfahl-tuer.info: A reed curtain and a ladder. Pull the ladder up at night and the house is a fortress, until the stilts rot.
texte.bk-pfahl-tuer.name: Stilt Plank Door
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-a.info: A crab trap hangs under the floor. What it catches depends on who fell off the walkway last night.
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-a.name: Stilt Plank Wall A
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-b.info: A fishing net drying on the wall. It has caught fish, crabs and one tax collector.
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-b.name: Stilt Plank Wall B
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-d.info: Five strokes and a red smear. The moneylender keeps his books on the debtor's wall.
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-d.name: Stilt Plank Wall D
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-oben-a.info: Two crab traps on pegs. The crabs pay rent in claws.
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-oben-a.name: Stilt Plank Upper Wall A
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-oben.info: More salt-grey planks, higher up, where the smell of the mudflats arrives a moment later.
texte.bk-pfahl-wand-oben.name: Stilt Plank Upper Wall
texte.bk-pfahl-wand.info: Salt-bleached planks on mangrove stilts. The tide comes in under the floor twice a day and takes whatever fell through the cracks.
texte.bk-pfahl-wand.name: Stilt Plank Wall

texte.bk-putz-fenster-a.info: Shutters closed tight, with a knothole at eye height. Someone up there is always watching.
texte.bk-putz-fenster-a.name: Whitewash Window A
texte.bk-putz-fenster-b.info: A pot of herbs on the sill. Dead since the last drought, still watered out of spite.
texte.bk-putz-fenster-b.name: Whitewash Window B
texte.bk-putz-fenster-c.info: Laundry on a line: a tunic, a loincloth, a rag of uncertain purpose. Nothing here is ever really clean.
texte.bk-putz-fenster-c.name: Whitewash Window C
texte.bk-putz-fenster-d.info: A birdcage on a nail. The bird stopped singing some time ago. Nobody noticed which day.
texte.bk-putz-fenster-d.name: Whitewash Window D
texte.bk-putz-fenster-e.info: A chamber pot on the sill, freshly emptied downwards. Look up before you walk below.
texte.bk-putz-fenster-e.name: Whitewash Window E
texte.bk-putz-fenster.info: An upper window with green shutters. From up here you can see the arena and smell the tannery.
texte.bk-putz-fenster.name: Whitewash Window
texte.bk-putz-giebel-a.info: A whitewashed gable with a dove hole. The doves are dinner, the droppings are décor.
texte.bk-putz-giebel-a.name: Whitewash Gable A
texte.bk-putz-giebel-ab.info: The falling verge, finished with a row of clay tiles. Rain runs straight into the neighbour's window.
texte.bk-putz-giebel-ab.name: Whitewash Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-putz-giebel-auf.info: The rising verge, finished with a row of clay tiles. Wind gets in anyway.
texte.bk-putz-giebel-auf.name: Whitewash Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-putz-giebel-b.info: A gable with a dove hole and the evidence running down from it.
texte.bk-putz-giebel-b.name: Whitewash Gable B
texte.bk-putz-giebel.info: A whitewashed gable. Pigeons rent it by the day.
texte.bk-putz-giebel.name: Whitewash Gable
texte.bk-putz-tuer-a.info: The door stands ajar. Either they trust the street or there is nothing left to steal.
texte.bk-putz-tuer-a.name: Whitewash Door A
texte.bk-putz-tuer-b.info: A red curtain instead of a door. Cheaper than wood and just as useless against thieves.
texte.bk-putz-tuer-b.name: Whitewash Door B
texte.bk-putz-tuer.info: An arched door of rough planks with iron studs. The studs are for the bailiff.
texte.bk-putz-tuer.name: Whitewash Door
texte.bk-putz-wand-a.info: A window with blue shutters, so the neighbours can watch the executions without paying.
texte.bk-putz-wand-a.name: Whitewash Wall A
texte.bk-putz-wand-b.info: The plaster has given up here. The bricks underneath are no better.
texte.bk-putz-wand-b.name: Whitewash Wall B
texte.bk-putz-wand-c.info: A small window and an iron ring for tethering a donkey, a goat or a debtor.
texte.bk-putz-wand-c.name: Whitewash Wall C
texte.bk-putz-wand-d.info: A crack and a wanted poster, already crossed out. The reward went to whoever brought the head.
texte.bk-putz-wand-d.name: Whitewash Wall D
texte.bk-putz-wand-e.info: A bloody handprint by the door. Someone was looking for the medicus and found the wall.
texte.bk-putz-wand-e.name: Whitewash Wall E
texte.bk-putz-wand-f.info: A wall shrine to Grumulus, god of locked doors. Someone stole his head; he never saw it coming.
texte.bk-putz-wand-f.name: Whitewash Wall F
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben-a.info: A small vent slit. It lets out the smoke and lets in the screams from the arena.
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben-a.name: Whitewash Upper Wall A
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben-b.info: Scaffold holes and a damp streak. The builders left in a hurry, the damp never left.
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben-b.name: Whitewash Upper Wall B
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben-c.info: A patch of fresh plaster over an old crack. Nobody asks what was behind it.
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben-c.name: Whitewash Upper Wall C
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben.info: Plain whitewash on the upper floor. Up here the stains are older and the rent is lower.
texte.bk-putz-wand-oben.name: Whitewash Upper Wall
texte.bk-putz-wand.info: Whitewash over cheap brick on an ochre plinth. Every spring a fresh coat, every autumn fresh stains.
texte.bk-putz-wand.name: Whitewash Wall

texte.bk-rotlehm-fenster-b.info: A broken shutter. Through it you can watch the cattle market, or be watched by it.

texte.bk-rotlehm-fenster-d.info: The shutter hangs on one strap. Tally marks below count debts, not days.

texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-a.name: Red Daub Wall A
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-b.info: Cracked in the dry season, cracked again in the wet. Ants rent the gap by the night.
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-b.name: Red Daub Wall B
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-d.info: A bleached cattle skull nailed by the door. The owner says it keeps lions away. No lions have complained.
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-d.name: Red Daub Wall D
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-oben-a.info: A clay nest under the beam. Rent is paid on the wall below.
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-oben-a.name: Red Daub Upper Wall A
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-oben.info: Upper daub under the eaves, zigzag and all. Swallows dirty it faster than the painter can.
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand-oben.name: Red Daub Upper Wall
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand.info: Red earth, dung and spit, slapped on thick. The white zigzags are for luck; the luck is not included.
texte.bk-rotlehm-wand.name: Red Daub Wall
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach-a.info: A smoke hole ringed with stones. Warmth goes out, snow comes in, the family stays in between.
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach-a.name: Sod Roof, Flat A
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach-b.info: Tent poles and hides laid out on the roof to dry. Moving house here means moving the roof.
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach-b.name: Sod Roof, Flat B
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach-d.info: A bleached horned skull on the roof. It keeps away evil spirits and, judging by the silence, the neighbours.
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach-d.name: Sod Roof, Flat D
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach.info: A flat roof of living turf. The goats would graze it, if anyone here still owned a goat.
texte.bk-sode-dach-flach.name: Sod Roof, Flat
texte.bk-sode-fenster-a.info: The gut pane split and was sewn up again. The stitches are better than the ones on the owner.
texte.bk-sode-fenster-a.name: Sod House Window A
texte.bk-sode-fenster-b.info: Boarded up for the winter. Winter lasts eleven months.
texte.bk-sode-fenster-b.name: Sod House Window B
texte.bk-sode-fenster-d.info: A horned skull over the boarded window. Either a charm or a warning about the cooking.
texte.bk-sode-fenster-d.name: Sod House Window D
texte.bk-sode-fenster.info: A pane of stretched gut. You cannot see through it, which is a mercy.
texte.bk-sode-fenster.name: Sod House Window
texte.bk-sode-tuer.info: A stone lintel and a hide flap. You enter bent over, which suits the local tax collector fine.
texte.bk-sode-tuer.name: Sod House Door
texte.bk-sode-wand-a.info: Reindeer antlers over the wall. Proof of a good hunt, or of a hungry winter.
texte.bk-sode-wand-a.name: Sod Wall A
texte.bk-sode-wand-b.info: A hide stretched on a drying frame. It used to be a reindeer, now it is a coat with prospects.
texte.bk-sode-wand-b.name: Sod Wall B
texte.bk-sode-wand-d.info: A slaughter hook, a frozen red trail and some bones. Out here, nothing is wasted and nothing is cleaned.
texte.bk-sode-wand-d.name: Sod Wall D
texte.bk-sode-wand-oben-a.info: Antlers on the upper floor as well. Somebody here is compensating.
texte.bk-sode-wand-oben-a.name: Sod Upper Wall A
texte.bk-sode-wand-oben.info: More turf, piled higher. Rich families can afford to be buried alive a little further from the ground.
texte.bk-sode-wand-oben.name: Sod Upper Wall
texte.bk-sode-wand.info: Stacked turf on a footing of field stones. Grass keeps growing in the wall, so the wall is technically a pasture.
texte.bk-sode-wand.name: Sod Wall
texte.bk-steppe-fenster-a.info: One shutter hangs by a single leather strap. The other went into the stove last February.
texte.bk-steppe-fenster-a.name: Steppe Wattle Window A
texte.bk-steppe-fenster-b.info: Stuffed with straw against the wind. Also against looking out, which helps.
texte.bk-steppe-fenster-b.name: Steppe Wattle Window B
texte.bk-steppe-fenster-d.info: A string of knucklebones in the window to scare off spirits. The spirits are reported to be unimpressed.
texte.bk-steppe-fenster-d.name: Steppe Wattle Window D
texte.bk-steppe-fenster.info: A hole with a shutter and ambitions. Lets in light, dust and the neighbours' arguments.
texte.bk-steppe-fenster.name: Steppe Wattle Window
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-a.info: Patched with a darker board and one hopeful nail.
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-a.name: Steppe Gable A
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-ab.info: The falling end of the gable boards. Gravity does most of the carpentry.
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-ab.name: Steppe Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-auf.info: The rising end of the gable boards, nailed down harder than the rest because the wind starts here.
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-auf.name: Steppe Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-b.info: A bundle of steppe grass tucked under the gable to dry. Tea, medicine or mattress, depending on the week.
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-b.name: Steppe Gable B
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-c.info: A plank kicked out in some argument. The draught won.
texte.bk-steppe-giebel-c.name: Steppe Gable C
texte.bk-steppe-giebel.info: Sun-bleached planks under the eaves. Every one of them was a fence post before somebody needed it more.
texte.bk-steppe-giebel.name: Steppe Gable
texte.bk-steppe-tuer.info: Planks, leather hinges and a horseshoe hung upside down so the luck drains out onto the doorstep, where it belongs.
texte.bk-steppe-tuer.name: Steppe Wattle Door
texte.bk-steppe-wand-a.info: The daub fell off and nobody noticed for three summers. The wattle underneath is holding up the house and its opinions.
texte.bk-steppe-wand-a.name: Steppe Wattle Wall A
texte.bk-steppe-wand-b.info: Dung cakes drying on the wall: winter fuel, summer perfume. Out here even the smoke is second-hand.
texte.bk-steppe-wand-b.name: Steppe Wattle Wall B
texte.bk-steppe-wand-d.info: A horse skull nailed up for luck. It did not bring the horse much, either.
texte.bk-steppe-wand-d.name: Steppe Wattle Wall D
texte.bk-steppe-wand-oben-a.info: A hide stretched out to dry. Whose hide, the family declines to say.
texte.bk-steppe-wand-oben-a.name: Steppe Wattle Upper Wall A
texte.bk-steppe-wand-oben.info: Upper floor of wattle and daub, built by someone who had seen a second storey once, from a distance.
texte.bk-steppe-wand-oben.name: Steppe Wattle Upper Wall
texte.bk-steppe-wand.info: Wattle, clay and a skirt of grass sods. The wind gets in anyway; so does the tax man.
texte.bk-steppe-wand.name: Steppe Wattle Wall
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster-a.info: A gourd and a pot of brackish water on the sill. The water is for drinking. Good luck.
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster-a.name: Reed Stilt Window A
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster-b.info: The mat is down. Whoever lives here owes someone money, or a finger.
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster-b.name: Reed Stilt Window B
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster-d.info: A red rag over the shutter: swamp fever. The healer charges double for houses like this, payable in advance.
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster-d.name: Reed Stilt Window D
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster.info: A hole with a mat rolled above it. The mosquitoes use it as their main entrance.
texte.bk-sumpf-fenster.name: Reed Stilt Window
texte.bk-sumpf-tuer.info: A rolled-up mat and one wobbly step. Visitors are announced by the splash.
texte.bk-sumpf-tuer.name: Reed Stilt Door
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-a.info: A hole plugged with swamp mud and a cushion of moss. Wall repair, the local way.
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-a.name: Reed Stilt Wall A
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-b.info: Bundles of herbs drying under the eaves. Half are for fever, half cause it.
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-b.name: Reed Stilt Wall B
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-d.info: A jawbone and a string of finger bones against evil spirits. The last tax collector donated them.
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-d.name: Reed Stilt Wall D
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-oben-a.info: Two eel traps hung out to dry. The eels did not volunteer either.
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-oben-a.name: Reed Stilt Upper Wall A
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-oben.info: Reed mats one floor up, slightly drier and considerably more expensive.
texte.bk-sumpf-wand-oben.name: Reed Stilt Upper Wall
texte.bk-sumpf-wand.info: Reed mats lashed to rotten posts above the swamp. The damp climbs the wall faster than the rent.
texte.bk-sumpf-wand.name: Reed Stilt Wall
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-a.info: Cracked by the sun. One more good rain and the bedroom gets a skylight.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-a.name: Mudbrick Roof A
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-b.info: Fresh mud, laid last month. Already looks a hundred years old.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-b.name: Mudbrick Roof B
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-c.info: Sand drifts in from the dunes every night. Sweeping it off is a job for the youngest debtor.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-c.name: Mudbrick Roof C
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-d.info: Three water jars cooling on the roof. Counted every morning, twice.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-d.name: Mudbrick Roof D
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-e.info: Dates drying on a palm mat. The flies got their share first.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-e.name: Mudbrick Roof E
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-f.info: A hatch and the tops of a ladder. Pull the ladder up and the house becomes a fortress, for an hour.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach-f.name: Mudbrick Roof F
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach.info: A flat roof of packed mud and straw. The family sleeps up here when the house gets too hot.
texte.bk-wueste-dach-flach.name: Mudbrick Roof
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-a.info: Shutters closed against the noon sun, the sandstorm and the neighbours.
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-a.name: Mudbrick Window A
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-b.info: A red rag hangs out to dry next to a pot of herbs. Both have seen better days.
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-b.name: Mudbrick Window B
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-c.info: A string of dried peppers. Hot enough to keep away flies, guests and the evil eye.
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-c.name: Mudbrick Window C
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-d.info: Bricked up and marked with a charcoal cross. Whatever was inside is not coming out.
texte.bk-wueste-fenster-d.name: Mudbrick Window D
texte.bk-wueste-fenster.info: A small window behind a wooden lattice. Lets in a little air and a lot of gossip.
texte.bk-wueste-fenster.name: Mudbrick Window
texte.bk-wueste-tuer-a.info: A torn notice is nailed to the door. Nobody here can read it, which is probably for the best.
texte.bk-wueste-tuer-a.name: Mudbrick Door A
texte.bk-wueste-tuer-b.info: A goat-hair blanket instead of a door. Wood is for the rich and the dead.
texte.bk-wueste-tuer-b.name: Mudbrick Door B
texte.bk-wueste-tuer.info: Palm planks under a palm-log lintel. Locked at night, which only slows the tax collector down.
texte.bk-wueste-tuer.name: Mudbrick Door
texte.bk-wueste-wand-a.info: The plaster fell off years ago. Nobody replastered it, the bricks look honest enough.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-a.name: Mudbrick Wall A
texte.bk-wueste-wand-b.info: A crack, smeared shut with fresh mud. Repeat every spring until the house wins.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-b.name: Mudbrick Wall B
texte.bk-wueste-wand-c.info: The one rain of the year left its tracks under every beam. Locals still talk about it.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-c.name: Mudbrick Wall C
texte.bk-wueste-wand-d.info: An iron ring and a short chain for a camel, a goat or a debtor. The stain below is from one of them.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-d.name: Mudbrick Wall D
texte.bk-wueste-wand-e.info: A niche with a water jar. Stealing from it is a hanging offence, drinking from it a gamble.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-e.name: Mudbrick Wall E
texte.bk-wueste-wand-f.info: A water jar broke here. The wet patch is the most valuable thing in the street.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-f.name: Mudbrick Wall F
texte.bk-wueste-wand-oben-a.info: A wooden spout drains the roof. It has done so twice in living memory.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-oben-a.name: Mudbrick Upper Wall A
texte.bk-wueste-wand-oben-b.info: A coil of rope on a peg, ready for the well, the camel or the thief.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-oben-b.name: Mudbrick Upper Wall B
texte.bk-wueste-wand-oben.info: The upper floor, mud on mud. Every storey is a bet against the next earthquake.
texte.bk-wueste-wand-oben.name: Mudbrick Upper Wall
texte.bk-wueste-wand.info: Sun-baked mud, palm beams poking out at the top. Holds up the roof and, on a good day, itself.
texte.bk-wueste-wand.name: Mudbrick Wall
texte.bk-ziegel-boden.info: Terracotta tiles, red and buff. They hide wine stains well and blood even better.
texte.bk-ziegel-boden.name: Brick Floor
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i-a.info: Moss has settled between the tiles. It pays no rent either.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i-a.name: Tiled Right A
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i-d.info: A missing tile, covered with a plank and two nails. Good until the next storm, as everything is.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i-d.name: Tiled Right D
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Right
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j-a.info: Moss has settled between the tiles. It pays no rent either.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j-a.name: Tiled Front A
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j-d.info: A missing tile, covered with a plank and two nails. Good until the next storm, as everything is.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j-d.name: Tiled Front D
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Front
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i-a.info: Moss has settled between the tiles. It pays no rent either.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i-a.name: Tiled Left A
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i-d.info: A missing tile, covered with a plank and two nails. Good until the next storm, as everything is.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i-d.name: Tiled Left D
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Left
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j-a.info: Moss has settled between the tiles. It pays no rent either.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j-a.name: Tiled Rear A
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j-d.info: A missing tile, covered with a plank and two nails. Good until the next storm, as everything is.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j-d.name: Tiled Rear D
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Rear
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach-a.info: Moss has settled between the tiles. It pays no rent either.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach-a.name: Tiled Flat A
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach-d.info: A missing tile, covered with a plank and two nails. Good until the next storm, as everything is.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach-d.name: Tiled Flat D
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach.info: A flat tiled roof. In summer the family sleeps up here, in winter the cat.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach.name: Tiled Roof, Flat
texte.bk-ziegel-fenster.info: A window in a brick frame with green shutters. Ideal for emptying pots onto passers-by.
texte.bk-ziegel-fenster.name: Brick Window
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-ab.info: The falling half of a plastered gable. Rain runs down it and into the neighbour's window.
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-ab.name: Brick Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-auf.info: The peak of a plastered gable. The highest point of the house and of the landlord's ambitions.
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-auf.name: Brick Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel.info: A plastered gable wall. Pigeons rent it by the day.
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel.name: Brick Gable
texte.bk-ziegel-rang.info: Tiers of stone seats. Bring a cushion, or rent one at a price that hurts more than the stone.
texte.bk-ziegel-rang.name: Brick Tiers
texte.bk-ziegel-schild.info: A painted signboard with a red frame. It promises quality and is right about half the time.
texte.bk-ziegel-schild.name: Brick Sign
texte.bk-ziegel-tuer.info: A wooden door under a brick lintel. Knock twice; the third knock is always the debt collector.
texte.bk-ziegel-tuer.name: Brick Door
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-a.info: The plaster has let go and the bricks show through. The landlord calls it rustic charm.
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-a.name: Brick Wall A
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-b.info: A list of names scratched in charcoal, each with a tally. Not a guest list. Nobody on it is invited anywhere.
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-b.name: Brick Wall B
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-d.info: A bloody handprint at shoulder height. Someone leaned here on the way out of a dispute.
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-d.name: Brick Wall D
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-oben.info: An upper floor of plastered brick. The higher the floor, the cheaper the tenant and the longer the fall.
texte.bk-ziegel-wand-oben.name: Brick Upper Wall
texte.bk-ziegel-wand.info: Plastered brick on a red plinth. Respectable enough to have debts.
texte.bk-ziegel-wand.name: Brick Wall
texte.blume-distel.info: A thistle with a purple crown. It stabs everyone who touches it and has never lost a fight.
texte.blume-distel.name: Thistle
texte.blume-hohes-gras.info: Grass up to the hip, dry and golden. Whatever hunts in it can see you long before you see it.
texte.blume-hohes-gras.name: Tall Grass
texte.blume-schilf.info: Reeds at the edge of the water. Good for roofs, baskets and for losing a sandal.
texte.blume-schilf.name: Reeds
texte.blume-wiese.info: A handful of wildflowers. Pretty, harmless and trampled within the week.
texte.blume-wiese.name: Wildflowers
texte.boden-erde.info: Honest dirt with a few pebbles. Everything you own will end up in it, and so will you.
texte.boden-erde.name: Bare Earth
texte.boden-fels.info: Solid rock. Nothing grows here and nothing can be buried here, which makes it popular with neither farmers nor undertakers.
texte.boden-fels.name: Bedrock
texte.boden-fluss-a.info: Swift, cold and in a hurry, like a debtor who just saw the gate open.
texte.boden-fluss-a.name: River (current)
texte.boden-fluss-b.info: The froth is natural. Mostly. The tanners say so, and they should know.
texte.boden-fluss-b.name: River (foam)
texte.boden-fluss-c.info: A barrel heading downstream. Wine, nails or a tax collector; nobody fishes it out to check.
texte.boden-fluss-c.name: River (drifting barrel)
texte.boden-fluss-d.info: Belly up and still the best swimmer in the city.
texte.boden-fluss-d.name: River (dead rat)
texte.boden-fluss.info: Brown in the cities, blue on the maps. Downstream, everyone drinks what upstream washed off.
texte.boden-fluss.name: River
texte.boden-gras.info: Grass. It grows on anything, including last season's losers.
texte.boden-gras.name: Grass
texte.boden-muellgrube-n.info: The district's only public institution. It takes everything and never asks for papers.
texte.boden-muellgrube-n.name: Refuse Pit
texte.boden-muellgrube-o.info: A victory wreath lies on top. Somebody won something once and found out what it was worth.
texte.boden-muellgrube-o.name: Refuse Pit
texte.boden-muellgrube-s.info: The black puddle at the bottom has been there longer than the district. It may own it.
texte.boden-muellgrube-s.name: Refuse Pit
texte.boden-muellgrube-w.info: Dug by the residents, filled by the residents. The only project they ever finished.
texte.boden-muellgrube-w.name: Refuse Pit
texte.boden-sand.info: Fine sand, excellent at soaking up whatever gets spilled on it. The arena uses the same kind, for the same reason.
texte.boden-sand.name: Sand
texte.boden-schlamm-bretter.info: Two planks over the mud. The only paved road in the district, and somebody owns it.
texte.boden-schlamm-bretter.name: Plank Walk
texte.boden-schlamm-matsch.info: Mud, deep enough to keep a sandal and give back only the foot.
texte.boden-schlamm-matsch.name: Slum Mud
texte.boden-schlamm-oel.info: A puddle with a rainbow on top. Nobody asks what made the rainbow.
texte.boden-schlamm-oel.name: Greasy Puddle
texte.boden-schlamm-pfuetze.info: Brown puddles that never dry. Children call them the sea. The sea would sue.
texte.boden-schlamm-pfuetze.name: Slum Puddles
texte.boden-schlamm-rinne.info: An open gutter carries everything downhill to the neighbours. They return the favour.
texte.boden-schlamm-rinne.name: Open Gutter
texte.boden-schlamm-scherben.info: Broken pots and pebbles. Every step is an archaeology lesson with blood.
texte.boden-schlamm-scherben.name: Shards in Mud
texte.boden-schlamm-spur.info: Cart ruts full of brown water. The cart left years ago; the ruts stayed for the rent.
texte.boden-schlamm-spur.name: Slum Ruts
texte.boden-schlamm-stroh.info: Straw thrown on the mud to make it walkable. It made it smell instead.
texte.boden-schlamm-stroh.name: Trodden Straw
texte.boden-wasser.info: Fresh water, more or less. The men drink from it, the oxen stand in it, and nobody asks in which order.
texte.boden-wasser.name: Waterhole
texte.boden-weg.info: Packed earth with two cart ruts. Carts love it; whoever falls asleep on it will not love the carts.
texte.boden-weg.name: Dirt Road
texte.bruch-hebebaum.info: Three poles, a pulley and a winch. It lifts a block a hand high and keeps everybody's feet out from under it.
texte.bruch-hebebaum.name: Lifting Tripod
texte.bruch-keilblock.info: Iron wedges in a row, waiting for the hammer. One hole is empty; the wedge is in somebody's boot.
texte.bruch-keilblock.name: Wedged Block
texte.bruch-quader-a.info: Blocks on a timber sledge, ready to be dragged. One lost a corner on the way; it will be sold as rustic.
texte.bruch-quader-a.name: Ashlars on Sledge
texte.bruch-quader.info: Squared blocks with the mason's mark. Each mark means one man's pay, so each mark is carved very large.
texte.bruch-quader.name: Ashlar Stack
texte.bruch-rohblock.info: A rough lump straight off the face. A crowbar, a wedge of wood and a prayer are all it takes to move it.
texte.bruch-rohblock.name: Rough Block
texte.bruch-splitt.info: Chips and dust under the crane, and half a chisel. The other half went somewhere when it broke.
texte.bruch-splitt.name: Stone Chips
texte.bruch-wand-1-nord.info: The quarry face, cut in steps. The wedges go in dry and come out wet; the stone splits along whatever line it likes.
texte.bruch-wand-1-nord.name: Quarry Face N
texte.bruch-wand-1-ost.info: The quarry face, cut in steps. The wedges go in dry and come out wet; the stone splits along whatever line it likes.
texte.bruch-wand-1-ost.name: Quarry Face E
texte.bruch-wand-1-sued.info: The quarry face, cut in steps. The wedges go in dry and come out wet; the stone splits along whatever line it likes.
texte.bruch-wand-1-sued.name: Quarry Face S
texte.bruch-wand-1-west.info: The quarry face, cut in steps. The wedges go in dry and come out wet; the stone splits along whatever line it likes.
texte.bruch-wand-1-west.name: Quarry Face W
texte.bruch-wand-2-nord.info: Where a block came out there is now a neat hole. A temple somewhere has a new step; the quarry has a new ladder.
texte.bruch-wand-2-nord.name: Quarry Face Pit N
texte.bruch-wand-2-ost.info: Where a block came out there is now a neat hole. A temple somewhere has a new step; the quarry has a new ladder.
texte.bruch-wand-2-ost.name: Quarry Face Pit E

texte.bruch-wand-2-west.info: Where a block came out there is now a neat hole. A temple somewhere has a new step; the quarry has a new ladder.
texte.bruch-wand-2-west.name: Quarry Face Pit W
texte.bruch-wand-3-nord.info: A block tipped back and cracked, the rope snapped, and the red stripe on the face is not ochre. The block was a write-off too.
texte.bruch-wand-3-nord.name: Quarry Face Slip N
texte.bruch-wand-3-ost.info: A block tipped back and cracked, the rope snapped, and the red stripe on the face is not ochre. The block was a write-off too.
texte.bruch-wand-3-ost.name: Quarry Face Slip E
texte.bruch-wand-3-sued.info: A block tipped back and cracked, the rope snapped, and the red stripe on the face is not ochre. The block was a write-off too.
texte.bruch-wand-3-sued.name: Quarry Face Slip S
texte.bruch-wand-3-west.info: A block tipped back and cracked, the rope snapped, and the red stripe on the face is not ochre. The block was a write-off too.
texte.bruch-wand-3-west.name: Quarry Face Slip W
texte.busch-banane.info: A banana plant with a hand of yellow fruit. The monkeys took the ripe ones and left you the bill.
texte.busch-banane.name: Banana Plant
texte.busch-bluete.info: A bush with orange blossoms. The bees adore it; the men use it for something less poetic.
texte.busch-bluete.name: Flowering Bush
texte.busch-gruen.info: A plain green bush. Just big enough to hide a coward, as several have already discovered.
texte.busch-gruen.name: Bush
texte.busch-hasel.info: A hazel shrub. Nuts in autumn, switches all year round.
texte.busch-hasel.name: Hazel
texte.busch-tamariske.info: A pale tamarisk that drinks the ground dry. Thrives where everything else gives up, which makes it the patron shrub of debtors.
texte.busch-tamariske.name: Tamarisk
texte.dach-ziegel.info: Red clay tiles over a plastered gable. Keeps the rain off the men and the men out of sight.
texte.dach-ziegel.name: Tiled Roof
texte.ehrensaeule-gestuerzt-i.info: History is written by the winners and edited with a hammer. Mind the drums.
texte.ehrensaeule-gestuerzt-i.name: Toppled Column I
texte.ehrensaeule-gestuerzt.info: Last year a hero, this year rubble. His name was chiselled off; his nose went the same way.
texte.ehrensaeule-gestuerzt.name: Toppled Column
texte.ehrensaeule-schande-i.info: The iron collar is empty today. The crow is optimistic.
texte.ehrensaeule-schande-i.name: Column of Shame I
texte.ehrensaeule-schande.info: Debtors and bad poets are chained here for the public to admire. Rotten fruit is sold at the next stall.
texte.ehrensaeule-schande.name: Column of Shame
texte.ehrensaeule-statue-i.info: The benefactor raises his hand to bless the market. Or to point out who still owes him money.
texte.ehrensaeule-statue-i.name: Column of Honour I
texte.ehrensaeule-statue.info: A grateful city honours its benefactor, who paid for the column, the statue and the gratitude. The pigeons add their own tribute.
texte.ehrensaeule-statue.name: Column of Honour
texte.elend-bude-1-nord.info: Boards, a rag for a door and three stones to keep the roof from leaving. The rent is collected anyway.
texte.elend-bude-1-nord.name: Plank Shack N
texte.elend-bude-1-ost.info: Boards, a rag for a door and three stones to keep the roof from leaving. The rent is collected anyway.
texte.elend-bude-1-ost.name: Plank Shack E
texte.elend-bude-1-sued.info: Boards, a rag for a door and three stones to keep the roof from leaving. The rent is collected anyway.
texte.elend-bude-1-sued.name: Plank Shack S
texte.elend-bude-1-west.info: Boards, a rag for a door and three stones to keep the roof from leaving. The rent is collected anyway.
texte.elend-bude-1-west.name: Plank Shack W
texte.elend-bude-2-nord.info: Reed mats patched with mud. Keeps out the sun, the rain and most of the neighbours. Not the smell.
texte.elend-bude-2-nord.name: Reed Hut N
texte.elend-bude-2-ost.info: Reed mats patched with mud. Keeps out the sun, the rain and most of the neighbours. Not the smell.
texte.elend-bude-2-ost.name: Reed Hut E
texte.elend-bude-2-sued.info: Reed mats patched with mud. Keeps out the sun, the rain and most of the neighbours. Not the smell.
texte.elend-bude-2-sued.name: Reed Hut S
texte.elend-bude-2-west.info: Reed mats patched with mud. Keeps out the sun, the rain and most of the neighbours. Not the smell.
texte.elend-bude-2-west.name: Reed Hut W
texte.elend-bude-3-nord.info: Mud walls stuffed with broken amphorae. The wine is long gone; the jars still work hard.
texte.elend-bude-3-nord.name: Shard House N
texte.elend-bude-3-ost.info: Mud walls stuffed with broken amphorae. The wine is long gone; the jars still work hard.
texte.elend-bude-3-ost.name: Shard House E
texte.elend-bude-3-sued.info: Mud walls stuffed with broken amphorae. The wine is long gone; the jars still work hard.
texte.elend-bude-3-sued.name: Shard House S
texte.elend-bude-3-west.info: Mud walls stuffed with broken amphorae. The wine is long gone; the jars still work hard.
texte.elend-bude-3-west.name: Shard House W
texte.elend-bude-4-nord.info: A stolen sail on two sticks makes a porch. Somebody sits here all day and calls it business.
texte.elend-bude-4-nord.name: Shack with Awning N
texte.elend-bude-4-ost.info: A stolen sail on two sticks makes a porch. Somebody sits here all day and calls it business.
texte.elend-bude-4-ost.name: Shack with Awning E
texte.elend-bude-4-sued.info: A stolen sail on two sticks makes a porch. Somebody sits here all day and calls it business.
texte.elend-bude-4-sued.name: Shack with Awning S
texte.elend-bude-4-west.info: A stolen sail on two sticks makes a porch. Somebody sits here all day and calls it business.
texte.elend-bude-4-west.name: Shack with Awning W
texte.elend-bude-5-nord.info: Planks, reeds, a red cloak nobody will ask about. A barrel catches the rain and the drowned flies.
texte.elend-bude-5-nord.name: Patchwork Shack N
texte.elend-bude-5-ost.info: Planks, reeds, a red cloak nobody will ask about. A barrel catches the rain and the drowned flies.
texte.elend-bude-5-ost.name: Patchwork Shack E
texte.elend-bude-5-sued.info: Planks, reeds, a red cloak nobody will ask about. A barrel catches the rain and the drowned flies.
texte.elend-bude-5-sued.name: Patchwork Shack S
texte.elend-bude-5-west.info: Planks, reeds, a red cloak nobody will ask about. A barrel catches the rain and the drowned flies.
texte.elend-bude-5-west.name: Patchwork Shack W
texte.elend-bude-6-nord.info: Built from a fishmonger's sign nailed on upside down. FRESH, it promises. It is not.
texte.elend-bude-6-nord.name: Shack of Old Signs N
texte.elend-bude-6-ost.info: Built from a fishmonger's sign nailed on upside down. FRESH, it promises. It is not.
texte.elend-bude-6-ost.name: Shack of Old Signs E
texte.elend-bude-6-sued.info: Built from a fishmonger's sign nailed on upside down. FRESH, it promises. It is not.
texte.elend-bude-6-sued.name: Shack of Old Signs S
texte.elend-bude-6-west.info: Built from a fishmonger's sign nailed on upside down. FRESH, it promises. It is not.
texte.elend-bude-6-west.name: Shack of Old Signs W
texte.elend-bude-7-nord.info: Held up by one beam, one rope and stubbornness. Do not lean on it. Do not sneeze near it.
texte.elend-bude-7-nord.name: Sagging Shack N
texte.elend-bude-7-ost.info: Held up by one beam, one rope and stubbornness. Do not lean on it. Do not sneeze near it.
texte.elend-bude-7-ost.name: Sagging Shack E
texte.elend-bude-7-sued.info: Held up by one beam, one rope and stubbornness. Do not lean on it. Do not sneeze near it.

texte.elend-bude-8-nord.info: Door nailed shut, a red hand and a notice. The landlord got the hut back. The tenant got the street.
texte.elend-bude-8-nord.name: Evicted Shack N
texte.elend-bude-8-ost.info: Door nailed shut, a red hand and a notice. The landlord got the hut back. The tenant got the street.
texte.elend-bude-8-ost.name: Evicted Shack E
texte.elend-bude-8-sued.info: Door nailed shut, a red hand and a notice. The landlord got the hut back. The tenant got the street.

texte.elend-bude-8-west.name: Evicted Shack W
texte.elend-erbrochen-1.name: Vomit
texte.elend-erbrochen-2.info: Next to it the cup of the finest local wine. The stomach disagreed with the label.
texte.elend-erbrochen-2.name: Vomit and Cup
texte.elend-hasch-nord.info: Hemp drying, a press squeezing, a wall full of chalk debts. Everybody here is relaxed except the creditor.
texte.elend-hasch-nord.name: Hash Press N
texte.elend-hasch-ost.info: Hemp drying, a press squeezing, a wall full of chalk debts. Everybody here is relaxed except the creditor.
texte.elend-hasch-ost.name: Hash Press E
texte.elend-hasch-sued.info: Hemp drying, a press squeezing, a wall full of chalk debts. Everybody here is relaxed except the creditor.
texte.elend-hasch-sued.name: Hash Press S
texte.elend-hasch-west.info: Hemp drying, a press squeezing, a wall full of chalk debts. Everybody here is relaxed except the creditor.
texte.elend-hasch-west.name: Hash Press W
texte.elend-karren.info: One wheel left, the other sold. It still carries a load: the rags of its owner.
texte.elend-karren.name: Broken Handcart
texte.elend-knochen-1.info: Gnawed clean. The dogs came second.
texte.elend-knochen-1.name: Bones
texte.elend-knochen-2.info: A goat once. Then dinner. Now a xylophone for children.
texte.elend-knochen-2.name: Ribcage
texte.elend-knochen-3.info: Dipped for a coin, pulled out for the next pot. Flavour guaranteed for another week.
texte.elend-knochen-3.name: Soup Bone on a String
texte.elend-knochenhaufen-1.info: The leftovers of the cookshops. Soup has been made of them twice already.
texte.elend-knochenhaufen-1.name: Bone Heap
texte.elend-knochenhaufen-2.info: Bones for soup, bones for dice. The house always wins, and the house is a heap.
texte.elend-knochenhaufen-2.name: Bone Heap with Dice
texte.elend-kochstelle-1.info: Stones, ashes and a kettle. The fire is out because the wood was eaten.
texte.elend-kochstelle-1.name: Cold Fire Pit
texte.elend-kochstelle-2.info: SOUP, says the board. A bone in the pot argues the point.
texte.elend-kochstelle-2.name: Soup Kettle
texte.elend-kot-1.info: Nobody owns a latrine here. Everybody owns a corner.
texte.elend-kot-1.name: Droppings
texte.elend-kot-2.info: A little sign says NOT. The rest of the sentence was stepped on.
texte.elend-kot-2.name: Droppings with Sign
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-nord.info: Bark-edged offcuts the sawmill threw away, a sack for a door. The sawmill charges rent for the offcuts.
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-nord.name: Slab Shack N
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-ost.info: Bark-edged offcuts the sawmill threw away, a sack for a door. The sawmill charges rent for the offcuts.
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-ost.name: Slab Shack E
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-sued.info: Bark-edged offcuts the sawmill threw away, a sack for a door. The sawmill charges rent for the offcuts.
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-sued.name: Slab Shack S
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-west.info: Bark-edged offcuts the sawmill threw away, a sack for a door. The sawmill charges rent for the offcuts.
texte.elend-laub-bude-1-west.name: Slab Shack W
texte.elend-laub-bude-2-nord.info: Bark walls and a roof of turf. Grows mushrooms, moss and coughs in roughly equal measure.
texte.elend-laub-bude-2-nord.name: Bark Hut N
texte.elend-laub-bude-2-ost.info: Bark walls and a roof of turf. Grows mushrooms, moss and coughs in roughly equal measure.
texte.elend-laub-bude-2-ost.name: Bark Hut E

texte.elend-laub-bude-2-west.name: Bark Hut W
texte.elend-laub-bude-3-nord.info: Sticks and mud, like a bird nest for people who could not afford a tree.
texte.elend-laub-bude-3-nord.name: Wattle Hut N
texte.elend-laub-bude-3-ost.info: Sticks and mud, like a bird nest for people who could not afford a tree.
texte.elend-laub-bude-3-ost.name: Wattle Hut E

texte.elend-laub-bude-3-west.name: Wattle Hut W

texte.elend-laub-bude-4-nord.name: Firewood Stall Shack N
texte.elend-laub-bude-4-ost.info: Sells firewood from under a sack awning. The forest is free; the sitting is the business.
texte.elend-laub-bude-4-ost.name: Firewood Stall Shack E
texte.elend-laub-bude-4-sued.info: Sells firewood from under a sack awning. The forest is free; the sitting is the business.

texte.elend-laub-bude-4-west.info: Sells firewood from under a sack awning. The forest is free; the sitting is the business.
texte.elend-laub-bude-4-west.name: Firewood Stall Shack W
texte.elend-laub-bude-5-nord.info: Planks, bark, sacking and a red cloak nobody asks about. The barrel catches rain and beetles.
texte.elend-laub-bude-5-nord.name: Patchwork Hovel N
texte.elend-laub-bude-5-ost.info: Planks, bark, sacking and a red cloak nobody asks about. The barrel catches rain and beetles.
texte.elend-laub-bude-5-ost.name: Patchwork Hovel E

texte.elend-laub-bude-5-west.name: Patchwork Hovel W

texte.elend-laub-bude-6-nord.name: Shack of Old Signs N
texte.elend-laub-bude-6-ost.info: Built from a timber merchant's sign nailed on upside down. It still advertises honest measures.

texte.elend-laub-bude-7-nord.name: Sinking Hut N
texte.elend-laub-bude-7-ost.info: Propped up by one branch and stubbornness. The moss is winning. Do not sneeze inside.
texte.elend-laub-bude-7-ost.name: Sinking Hut E

texte.elend-laub-bude-7-west.name: Sinking Hut W
texte.elend-laub-bude-8-nord.info: Door nailed shut, a red hand, a notice and an axe left in the stump. The landlord kept the hut. The forest keeps the rest.
texte.elend-laub-bude-8-nord.name: Evicted Hut N
texte.elend-laub-bude-8-ost.info: Door nailed shut, a red hand, a notice and an axe left in the stump. The landlord kept the hut. The forest keeps the rest.
texte.elend-laub-bude-8-ost.name: Evicted Hut E
