texte.elend-lumpen.info: A mat, a stone for a pillow, and a cup for the rain. Rent: free until somebody bigger comes.
texte.elend-lumpen.name: Rag Bed
texte.elend-muell-1.info: What the city throws away, the slum sorts. What the slum throws away is this.
texte.elend-muell-1.name: Rubbish Heap
texte.elend-muell-2.info: A basket gave up. The rubbish now has more room and the street has less.
texte.elend-muell-2.name: Spilled Rubbish
texte.elend-muell-3.info: On top lies a tax demand, torn in two. The tax collector will come back for both halves.
texte.elend-muell-3.name: Rubbish with Tax Notice
texte.elend-opium-nord.info: CURES ALL, says the board, and it does: pain, hunger, hope and eventually the customer. Paid in advance.
texte.elend-opium-nord.name: Opium Kitchen N
texte.elend-opium-ost.info: CURES ALL, says the board, and it does: pain, hunger, hope and eventually the customer. Paid in advance.
texte.elend-opium-ost.name: Opium Kitchen E
texte.elend-opium-sued.info: CURES ALL, says the board, and it does: pain, hunger, hope and eventually the customer. Paid in advance.
texte.elend-opium-sued.name: Opium Kitchen S
texte.elend-opium-west.info: CURES ALL, says the board, and it does: pain, hunger, hope and eventually the customer. Paid in advance.
texte.elend-opium-west.name: Opium Kitchen W
texte.elend-schrein-1.info: Our Lady of Leftovers, built from what she was given. She answers no prayers but keeps all offerings.
texte.elend-schrein-1.name: Shrine of the Gutter God
texte.elend-schrein-2.info: The offering box is locked. The priest has the key. The goddess does not.
texte.elend-schrein-2.name: Shrine with Offering Box
texte.elend-schuldpfahl.info: Every chalk line is a debt. When the post is full, the debtor is sold to pay for the chalk.
texte.elend-schuldpfahl.name: Debt Post
texte.elend-waesche-1.info: Rags hung out to dry. In the slum they get wetter.
texte.elend-waesche-1.name: Washing Line
texte.elend-waesche-2.info: A senator's toga, purple stripe and all. It fell off a cart. Twice.
texte.elend-waesche-2.name: Line with a Toga
texte.elend-wasser-1.info: Rain water, barrel water, puddle water. Drink fast and do not look.
texte.elend-wasser-1.name: Water Barrels
texte.elend-wasser-2.info: The sign promises CLEAN, MOSTLY. The shoe in the barrel promises nothing.
texte.elend-wasser-2.name: Clean Water Mostly
texte.feld-alraune-a.info: A fresh hole, a forked root and a torn rope on a stake. The rope did its job; the dog did not come back.
texte.feld-alraune-a.name: Mandrake Bed (dug up)
texte.feld-alraune.info: Dark star-shaped rosettes in black soil. Pull one up and you will hear about it. Briefly.
texte.feld-alraune.name: Mandrake Bed
texte.feld-bacchant-a.info: A puddle of wine and a dropped cup. It is wine. Probably.
texte.feld-bacchant-a.name: Bacchant Ground (puddle)
texte.feld-bacchant.info: Dark soil, purple stains and torn ribbons. Something was celebrated here, and nobody remembers what.
texte.feld-bacchant.name: Bacchant Ground
texte.feld-blumen-j.info: Flowers for garlands, temples and the graves of champions. Business is always blooming.
texte.feld-blumen-j.name: Flower Beds
texte.feld-blumen.info: Flowers for garlands, temples and the graves of champions. Business is always blooming.
texte.feld-blumen.name: Flower Beds
texte.feld-faerber-a.info: Somebody tipped the woad pot. The soil will be blue until the next emperor.
texte.feld-faerber-a.name: Dye Garden (spill)
texte.feld-faerber-j-a.info: Somebody tipped the woad pot. The soil will be blue until the next emperor.
texte.feld-faerber-j-a.name: Dye Garden (spill)
texte.feld-faerber-j.info: Madder for red, woad for blue. Senators wear the colours, the dyers wear the stains.
texte.feld-faerber-j.name: Dye Garden
texte.feld-faerber.info: Madder for red, woad for blue. Senators wear the colours, the dyers wear the stains.
texte.feld-faerber.name: Dye Garden
texte.feld-garten-a.info: Gourds sunbathing between leeks. They will end up hollowed out, like the gardener.
texte.feld-garten-a.name: Market Garden B
texte.feld-garten-b.info: A hoe dropped mid-row and a cabbage with holes. The caterpillars won this round.
texte.feld-garten-b.name: Market Garden (hoe)
texte.feld-garten-j-a.info: Gourds sunbathing between leeks. They will end up hollowed out, like the gardener.
texte.feld-garten-j-a.name: Market Garden B
texte.feld-garten-j-b.info: A hoe dropped mid-row and a cabbage with holes. The caterpillars won this round.
texte.feld-garten-j-b.name: Market Garden (hoe)
texte.feld-garten-j.info: Cabbages, onions, leeks and turnips in tidy beds. The tidiest thing a slave will ever own is a bed of leeks.
texte.feld-garten-j.name: Market Garden
texte.feld-garten.info: Cabbages, onions, leeks and turnips in tidy beds. The tidiest thing a slave will ever own is a bed of leeks.
texte.feld-garten.name: Market Garden
texte.feld-gerste-a.info: Barley still green in patches. The brewer is already selling the beer.
texte.feld-gerste-a.name: Barley Field B
texte.feld-gerste-j-a.info: Barley still green in patches. The brewer is already selling the beer.
texte.feld-gerste-j-a.name: Barley Field B
texte.feld-gerste-j.info: Pale barley for bread, beer and gladiators. Gladiators are called barley men, and they hate it.
texte.feld-gerste-j.name: Barley Field
texte.feld-gerste.info: Pale barley for bread, beer and gladiators. Gladiators are called barley men, and they hate it.
texte.feld-gerste.name: Barley Field
texte.feld-hain-a.info: Windfall rotting in the dust. The overseer calls it waste, the slaves call it lunch.
texte.feld-hain-a.name: Orchard Floor B
texte.feld-hain-b.info: A tipped basket and a single sandal. The picker left in a hurry, the overseer followed with a stick.
texte.feld-hain-b.name: Orchard Floor (basket)
texte.feld-hain.info: Hard earth and dry grass under the trees. Every fallen fruit is counted and every missing one is somebody's fault.
texte.feld-hain.name: Orchard Floor
texte.feld-huelsen-a.info: Lentils in the sun. Cheap, filling and a reliable cause of unrest in the barracks.
texte.feld-huelsen-a.name: Bean and Lentil Beds B
texte.feld-huelsen-j-a.info: Lentils in the sun. Cheap, filling and a reliable cause of unrest in the barracks.
texte.feld-huelsen-j-a.name: Bean and Lentil Beds B
texte.feld-huelsen-j.info: Beans, lentils and chickpeas: the soldier's meal, the slave's meal, the senator's secret meal.
texte.feld-huelsen-j.name: Bean and Lentil Beds
texte.feld-huelsen.info: Beans, lentils and chickpeas: the soldier's meal, the slave's meal, the senator's secret meal.
texte.feld-huelsen.name: Bean and Lentil Beds
texte.feld-kraeuter-a.info: A little wooden label nobody can read anymore. The physician swears it said "not for soup".
texte.feld-kraeuter-a.name: Physic Garden (label)
texte.feld-kraeuter.info: Square beds of sage, rue, rosemary and marigold. Half of them heal, the other half are for inheritance matters.
texte.feld-kraeuter.name: Physic Garden
texte.feld-lavendel-j.info: Purple rows that smell of luxury. The bath houses need a lot of it to hide what they smell of.
texte.feld-lavendel-j.name: Lavender Field
texte.feld-lavendel.info: Purple rows that smell of luxury. The bath houses need a lot of it to hide what they smell of.
texte.feld-lavendel.name: Lavender Field
texte.feld-mohn-a.info: A small knife left among the capsules. The harvester took a nap. A long one.
texte.feld-mohn-a.name: Poppy Field (knife)
texte.feld-mohn-j-a.info: A small knife left among the capsules. The harvester took a nap. A long one.
texte.feld-mohn-j-a.name: Poppy Field (knife)
texte.feld-mohn-j.info: Pale poppies with scratched seed heads. The milk that drips out makes even the arena bearable.
texte.feld-mohn-j.name: Poppy Field
texte.feld-mohn.info: Pale poppies with scratched seed heads. The milk that drips out makes even the arena bearable.
texte.feld-mohn.name: Poppy Field
texte.feld-pferch-a.info: A feeding trough with a few wisps of hay. The animals eat first; the stable boy eats what is left.
texte.feld-pferch-a.name: Pen (trough)
texte.feld-pferch.info: Trampled mud, old straw and a puddle that never dries. Home sweet home for goats, donkeys and chickens.
texte.feld-pferch.name: Pen
texte.feld-rebe-a.info: Yellow leaves and trampled grapes. It looks like a massacre, and it is only the harvest.
texte.feld-rebe-a.name: Vineyard Soil B
texte.feld-rebe-j-a.info: Yellow leaves and trampled grapes. It looks like a massacre, and it is only the harvest.
texte.feld-rebe-j-a.name: Vineyard Soil B J
texte.feld-rebe-j.info: Hoed earth between the vines, mulched with straw. Wine starts here, in the dirt, like most fortunes.
texte.feld-rebe-j.name: Vineyard Soil J
texte.feld-rebe.info: Hoed earth between the vines, mulched with straw. Wine starts here, in the dirt, like most fortunes.
texte.feld-rebe.name: Vineyard Soil
texte.feld-safran-j.info: Crocus flowers picked one by one for three red threads each. Worth more than the hands that pick them.
texte.feld-safran-j.name: Saffron Field
texte.feld-safran.info: Crocus flowers picked one by one for three red threads each. Worth more than the hands that pick them.
texte.feld-safran.name: Saffron Field
texte.feld-weide-a.info: Close-cropped grass. Sheep eat it, wolves eat the sheep, the landlord eats the shepherd's wages.
texte.feld-weide-a.name: Pasture B
texte.feld-weide-b.info: Thistles the sheep refuse to eat. Smart sheep.
texte.feld-weide-b.name: Pasture (thistles)
texte.feld-weide-c.info: A salt stone licked smooth. Salt is so dear that the sheep are paid better than the legion.
texte.feld-weide-c.name: Pasture (salt lick)
texte.feld-weide-d.info: A sheep bell with a torn strap. The sheep is gone. The shepherd is next, once the owner finds out.
texte.feld-weide-d.name: Pasture (lost bell)
texte.feld-weide.info: Grass grazed short, a sheep path and the usual droppings. The sheep are counted daily, the shepherds only when missing.
texte.feld-weide.name: Pasture
texte.feld-weizen-a.info: Wheat waving politely. The tax collector already counted every ear.
texte.feld-weizen-a.name: Wheat Field B
texte.feld-weizen-b.info: Someone ran straight through the wheat. Debtors rarely take the road.
texte.feld-weizen-b.name: Wheat Field (trampled)
texte.feld-weizen-c.info: The crows took their share before the landlord could. Only the feathers paid tax.
texte.feld-weizen-c.name: Wheat Field (crows)
texte.feld-weizen-d.info: A sickle left in the stubble, a dark stain beside it. Harvest accidents are counted as harvest.
texte.feld-weizen-d.name: Wheat Field (sickle)
texte.feld-weizen-j-a.info: Wheat waving politely. The tax collector already counted every ear.
texte.feld-weizen-j-a.name: Wheat Field B
texte.feld-weizen-j-b.info: Someone ran straight through the wheat. Debtors rarely take the road.
texte.feld-weizen-j-b.name: Wheat Field (trampled)
texte.feld-weizen-j-c.info: The crows took their share before the landlord could. Only the feathers paid tax.
texte.feld-weizen-j-c.name: Wheat Field (crows)
texte.feld-weizen-j-d.info: A sickle left in the stubble, a dark stain beside it. Harvest accidents are counted as harvest.
texte.feld-weizen-j-d.name: Wheat Field (sickle)
texte.feld-weizen-j.info: Golden wheat in neat rows. It feeds the city, the city feeds the arena, the arena feeds on the city.
texte.feld-weizen-j.name: Wheat Field
texte.feld-weizen.info: Golden wheat in neat rows. It feeds the city, the city feeds the arena, the arena feeds on the city.
texte.feld-weizen.name: Wheat Field
texte.fels-block.info: A grey boulder that has not moved since the gods dropped it. Patient, silent and completely useless until someone brings a pickaxe.
texte.fels-block.name: Boulder
texte.fels-kante-i.info: The hill under the important people. It holds them up better than the people below do.
texte.fels-kante-i.name: Rock Terrace
texte.fels-kante-j.info: Bare rock, one step higher. Down here you pay rent, up there you collect it.
texte.fels-kante-j.name: Rock Terrace
texte.fels-treppe-n.info: Cut into the hill by convicts, worn smooth by priests, slippery for everybody else.
texte.fels-treppe-n.name: Rock Stairs
texte.fels-treppe-o.info: Cut into the hill by convicts, worn smooth by priests, slippery for everybody else.
texte.fels-treppe-o.name: Rock Stairs

texte.fels-treppe-s.name: Rock Stairs
texte.fels-treppe-w.info: Cut into the hill by convicts, worn smooth by priests, slippery for everybody else.
texte.fels-treppe-w.name: Rock Stairs
texte.fighting-pit.info: A sunken square of bloody sand and a ladder. The ladder only goes one way for most.
texte.fighting-pit.name: Fighting Pit
texte.figur-arbeiter.info: An ordinary man of the ludus in a simple tunic. He carries, saws and digs until the day somebody hands him a sword instead.
texte.figur-arbeiter.name: Worker
texte.fischer-boot-a.info: A hole in the hull, half nailed over with a plank. The plank came from the last boat, which also had a hole.
texte.fischer-boot-a.name: Patched Boat
texte.fischer-boot.info: A fishing boat keel-up on trestles, a pot of tar beside it. Boats are tarred every spring and prayed for every storm.
texte.fischer-boot.name: Upturned Boat
texte.fischer-netze.info: Nets drying on two poles, with cork floats and a tear nobody will admit to. Mending is women's work, said a man once.
texte.fischer-netze.name: Net Rack

texte.forum-gang-ecke-i0j0.name: Forum Corner Column I0J0

texte.hain-feige-a.name: Grove Fig (broken)
texte.hain-feige.info: A broad fig tree heavy with purple fruit. Senators eat the figs, the wasps eat the senators' leftovers.
texte.hain-feige.name: Grove Fig
texte.hain-mandel-a.info: The almonds are beaten down with a long pole. The method is also popular with debt collectors.
texte.hain-mandel-a.name: Grove Almond (pole)
texte.hain-mandel.info: A slender almond tree. The nuts are sweet, the bitter ones are sold to poisoners at a better price.
texte.hain-mandel.name: Grove Almond
texte.hain-olive-a.info: Its heaviest branch rests on a wooden crutch. The oldest worker on the estate, and the only one allowed one.
texte.hain-olive-a.name: Grove Olive (crutch)
texte.hain-olive-b.info: A ladder with a missing rung and a stain beneath it. The olives were picked anyway.
texte.hain-olive-b.name: Grove Olive (ladder)
texte.hain-olive.info: An old olive tree, pruned for the harvest. It has outlived three owners and will outlive the next.
texte.hain-olive.name: Grove Olive
texte.hain-stumpf.info: A stump with the axe still in it. The tree stopped bearing fruit; on this estate that is a capital offence.
texte.hain-stumpf.name: Felled Grove Tree
texte.hall-of-fallen.info: Names scratched in stone, then scratched out. Cold candles, wilted wreaths, one fresh grave waiting.
texte.hall-of-fallen.name: Hall of the Fallen

texte.hofpresse-wein-ost.name: Farm Winepress E

texte.holz-hackklotz.info: Block, maul and a pile of split firewood. The block has been hit more times than any gladiator alive.
texte.holz-hackklotz.name: Chopping Block
texte.holz-stapel-a.info: A log on the saw buck, a crosscut saw on the ground and a carpet of sawdust. Two men, one rhythm, frequent arguments.
texte.holz-stapel-a.name: Saw Buck
texte.holz-stapel.info: Trimmed logs held by stakes. Pull the wrong stake and the pile becomes the fastest thing in the camp.
texte.holz-stapel.name: Log Pile
texte.jagd-fallen.info: Two cages, a coil of snares and a deadfall on its trigger stick. Step around it; the last apprentice did not.
texte.jagd-fallen.name: Trap Pile
texte.jagd-fellrahmen.info: A hide laced into a frame and a scraping beam. Somewhere a forest is one animal lighter and the arena one costume richer.
texte.jagd-fellrahmen.name: Hide Frame
texte.jagd-raeucher.info: Strips of meat over a cold fire pit. The hunter smokes the meat, the meat smokes the hunter, and both end up leathery.
texte.jagd-raeucher.name: Smoking Rack
texte.karren-ochse.info: A cart with one ox and three sacks. The ox does the work and the driver takes the credit; the ox is used to it.
texte.karren-ochse.name: Ox Cart
texte.koehler-kohle.info: Fresh charcoal, light and black. It weighs a fifth of the wood it was and costs five times as much.
texte.koehler-kohle.name: Charcoal Heap
texte.koehler-loesche.info: Earth and turf to smother the kiln, and a barrel of water for the rest. The barrel is for the kiln; the burner can wait.
texte.koehler-loesche.name: Turf and Water
texte.koehler-meiler-a.info: The kiln burnt through on one side and has been patched with fresh turf. The shovel stayed where it fell.
texte.koehler-meiler-a.name: Kiln Burnt Through
texte.koehler-meiler.info: A dome of wood under earth and turf, smouldering for days. If it breathes too hard, the burner breathes too little.
texte.koehler-meiler.name: Charcoal Kiln
texte.koehler-meilerbau.info: Billets stacked around the centre pole like a tent of firewood. In a week it will be a sack of charcoal.
texte.koehler-meilerbau.name: Kiln Being Built
texte.koehler-saecke.info: Sacks of charcoal and a tally stick. The buyer counts the sacks, the burner counts the notches; neither agrees.
texte.koehler-saecke.name: Charcoal Sacks
texte.koenigspalast-banner-ohne-i.info: The royal banner. The crown was unpicked when the last king fell; the next one has not decided yet how big his should be.
texte.koenigspalast-banner-ohne-i.name: Royal Banner Blank I
texte.koenigspalast-banner-ohne.info: The royal banner. The crown was unpicked when the last king fell; the next one has not decided yet how big his should be.
texte.koenigspalast-banner-ohne.name: Royal Banner Blank
texte.koenigspalast-hinten-i.info: A golden gladiator on a modest plinth, propped up by two beams. The king says it is him. Nobody has said otherwise twice.
texte.koenigspalast-hinten-i.name: Royal Palace W
texte.koenigspalast-hinten.info: Behind the throne room the king feasts in his garden. The cage is empty; the lion is out, doing what lions and kings do best.
texte.koenigspalast-hinten.name: Royal Palace N
texte.koenigspalast-vorn-i.info: The dome is gold where the money lasted and bronze where it did not. The east wing waits for the next tax.
texte.koenigspalast-vorn-i.name: Royal Palace E
texte.koenigspalast-vorn.info: Built by thousands, enjoyed by one. Petitions are accepted at the gate and answered next year, every year.
texte.koenigspalast-vorn.name: Royal Palace
texte.lager-platz-a.info: Two barrels and a crate. One holds wine, one holds vinegar, and the label fell off years ago.
texte.lager-platz-a.name: Storage Spot A
texte.lager-platz-b.info: Grain sacks and an amphora. The weevils got here first and are not paying rent.
texte.lager-platz-b.name: Storage Spot B
texte.lager-platz-c.info: Firewood stacked by someone who will never be warm.
texte.lager-platz-c.name: Storage Spot C
texte.lager-platz-d.info: A crate of skulls, sorted by size. The arena sells everything, eventually.
texte.lager-platz-d.name: Storage Spot D
texte.lager-platz-e.info: Spare chains and a sack of grain with a rat on top. The rat lost the negotiation.
texte.lager-platz-e.name: Storage Spot E
texte.lager-platz.info: A pallet with crates and a sack. Everything here belongs to somebody, and that somebody is not the man carrying it.
texte.lager-platz.name: Storage Spot
texte.leiche.info: A fallen gladiator in a dark puddle. He lies here for a day so the next ones know what the purse costs; then the cart takes him.
texte.leiche.name: Corpse
texte.markt-stand.info: The slave trader's stall. Every morning he brings five new men in chains; whoever is left at dusk goes back on the road with him. No refunds.
texte.markt-stand.name: Slave Market
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-nord.info: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-nord.name: Animal Goods Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-ost.info: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-ost.name: Animal Goods Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-sued.info: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-sued.name: Animal Goods Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-west.info: Two butchers who share one stall and one cleaver. Whatever one of them sells, the other one is still looking for.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x1-west.name: Animal Goods Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-nord.info: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-nord.name: Animal Goods Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-ost.info: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-ost.name: Animal Goods Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-sued.info: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-sued.name: Animal Goods Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-west.info: A tent full of hides, bones, sausages and empty cages. EVERY PART, says the board. Except the part that ran off.
texte.marktstand-animals-2x2-west.name: Animal Goods Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-animals-a.info: Hides nailed to the back, a basket of bones and a few horns. Everything but the animal, and the soup is made of that.
texte.marktstand-animals-a.name: Animal Goods Stall B
texte.marktstand-animals-b.info: Sausages, a bloody block and pots of fat. The board says MEAT?, which is the most honest thing in the market.
texte.marktstand-animals-b.name: Animal Goods Stall C
texte.marktstand-animals-c.info: A big cage, bars bent outward, a torn chain. The sign says GONE. The vendor is looking for a new arm and a new bear.
texte.marktstand-animals-c.name: Animal Goods Stall D
texte.marktstand-animals.info: Empty cages, a basket of eggs, a bale of wool. The cages were full this morning. Nobody asks where it all went.
texte.marktstand-animals.name: Animal Goods Stall
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-nord.info: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-nord.name: Arena Supply Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-ost.info: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-ost.name: Arena Supply Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-sued.info: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-sued.name: Arena Supply Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-west.info: Sand on one side, coffins on the other. The lanistas buy both in one trip and save a walk.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x1-west.name: Arena Supply Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-nord.info: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-nord.name: Arena Supply Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-ost.info: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-ost.name: Arena Supply Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-sued.info: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-sued.name: Arena Supply Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-west.info: Coffins at the back, hooks in the middle, wreaths at the counter. The tent is laid out like a career.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-2x2-west.name: Arena Supply Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-a.info: Coffins, stacked and priced by the dozen. BULK, says the board. Lanistas never buy just one.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-a.name: Arena Supply Stall B
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-b.info: Nets, chains, a stretcher and drag hooks for the Gate of Death. Hooks are the bestseller; nets come back broken.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-b.name: Arena Supply Stall C
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-c.info: One victory wreath, five coffins. The board says ODDS and the stock agrees.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies-c.name: Arena Supply Stall D
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies.info: Sacks of fresh arena sand, rakes and red-rimmed buckets. Sand soaks up anything, so they sell a lot of it.
texte.marktstand-arena-supplies.name: Arena Supply Stall
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-nord.info: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-nord.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-ost.info: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-ost.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-sued.info: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-sued.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-west.info: Two smiths, one table, a long row of blades. BARELY USED: the previous owners barely got to use them.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x1-west.name: Arms & Armour Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-nord.info: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-nord.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-ost.info: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-ost.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-sued.info: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-sued.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-west.info: A tent of dented helmets, broken shields and swords with stories. WAR SURPLUS, though nobody remembers which war.
texte.marktstand-arms-2x2-west.name: Arms & Armour Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-arms-a.info: Spears in a barrel and a grindstone. Every blade sharpened on site, so the first owner never knew what hit him.
texte.marktstand-arms-a.name: Arms & Armour Stall B
texte.marktstand-arms-b.info: Breastplates and a heap of rings that used to be mail. Half price, because half of the last owner is still inside.
texte.marktstand-arms-b.name: Arms & Armour Stall C
texte.marktstand-arms-c.info: A helmet with a neat hole, a bloody sword and a broken one. MINT, says the board. A brave vendor.
texte.marktstand-arms-c.name: Arms & Armour Stall D
texte.marktstand-arms.info: Swords on a rack, dented shields and plumed helmets. USED, says the board. By whom is not mentioned.
texte.marktstand-arms.name: Arms & Armour Stall
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-nord.info: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-nord.name: Clothing Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-ost.info: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-ost.name: Clothing Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-sued.info: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-sued.name: Clothing Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-west.info: Tunics on two lines and a lot of linen. WASHED TWICE, says the board. Once was not enough.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x1-west.name: Clothing Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-nord.info: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-nord.name: Clothing Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-ost.info: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-ost.name: Clothing Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-sued.info: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-sued.name: Clothing Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-west.info: A tent of tunics with neat holes and a tub of pink water. ESTATE SALE: the estates are freshly buried.
texte.marktstand-clothing-2x2-west.name: Clothing Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-clothing-a.info: Bolts of cloth and one of purple, chained to the counter. The board says SILK. The cloth disagrees.
texte.marktstand-clothing-a.name: Clothing Stall B
texte.marktstand-clothing-b.info: Tunics with neat holes in them. AIRY, says the board, which is one way to describe a spear wound.
texte.marktstand-clothing-b.name: Clothing Stall C
texte.marktstand-clothing-c.info: A tub of pink water and a washboard. CLEAN, promises the board. The last tunic on the line has its doubts.
texte.marktstand-clothing-c.name: Clothing Stall D
texte.marktstand-clothing.info: Tunics on a line, folded linen and a pair of sandals. All second-hand. The first hand did not need them any more.
texte.marktstand-clothing.name: Clothing Stall
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-nord.info: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-nord.name: Crops Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-ost.info: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-ost.name: Crops Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-sued.info: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-sued.name: Crops Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-west.info: Baskets, crates, onion braids and a scale. ALMOST FRESH, which in the arena district counts as a promise.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x1-west.name: Crops Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-nord.info: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-nord.name: Crops Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-ost.info: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-ost.name: Crops Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-sued.info: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-sued.name: Crops Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-west.info: A big green tent of grain, cabbage and crates. FARM FRESH: the farm is behind the arena, where the sand is dumped.
texte.marktstand-crops-2x2-west.name: Crops Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-crops-a.info: Crates of apples, olives and lemons, with herbs drying at the back. CHEAP, says the board, and it tastes like it.
texte.marktstand-crops-a.name: Crops Stall B
texte.marktstand-crops-b.info: Grain, onions and a crooked scale with a stone under one pan. FAIR, says the board. To the vendor.
texte.marktstand-crops-b.name: Crops Stall C
texte.marktstand-crops-c.info: A mouldy heap in the corner and two baskets of the same. HALF PRICE. Still overpriced.
texte.marktstand-crops-c.name: Crops Stall D
texte.marktstand-crops.info: Cabbages, turnips, sacks of grain and onion braids. Grown on good soil; the battlefield next door keeps it rich.
texte.marktstand-crops.name: Crops Stall
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-nord.info: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-nord.name: Drink Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-ost.info: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-ost.name: Drink Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-sued.info: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-sued.name: Drink Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-west.info: Amphorae on one side, barrels on the other, one long bar between. WATERED WINE: at least they are honest.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x1-west.name: Drink Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-nord.info: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-nord.name: Drink Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-ost.info: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-ost.name: Drink Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-sued.info: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-sued.name: Drink Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-west.info: Barrels, a big jar of water and cups on every table. LAST ROUND, says the board, every round, until somebody dies.
texte.marktstand-drink-2x2-west.name: Drink Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-drink-a.info: Barrels, wineskins and a row of cups. BEER, says the board. Gladiators drink it before a fight and wish they had not.
texte.marktstand-drink-a.name: Drink Stall B
texte.marktstand-drink-b.info: A big jar of water, a ladle and something floating in it. WATER, says the board. Mostly.
texte.marktstand-drink-b.name: Drink Stall C
texte.marktstand-drink-c.info: A barrel on its side, a purple puddle and eleven chalk marks for credit. CASH, says the board now.
texte.marktstand-drink-c.name: Drink Stall D
texte.marktstand-drink.info: Sealed amphorae, cups and a jug of the good stuff. The good stuff and the cheap stuff come from the same jug.
texte.marktstand-drink.name: Drink Stall
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-nord.info: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-nord.name: Exotic Food Double Stall N
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-ost.info: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-ost.name: Exotic Food Double Stall E
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-sued.info: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-sued.name: Exotic Food Double Stall S
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-west.info: Spices on one side, skewers on the other. ASK NOTHING, says the board, and the regulars never do.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x1-west.name: Exotic Food Double Stall W
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-nord.info: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-nord.name: Exotic Food Market Tent N
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-ost.info: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-ost.name: Exotic Food Market Tent E
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-sued.info: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-sued.name: Exotic Food Market Tent S
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-west.info: A tent of jars, kettles and coloured cones. NO REFUNDS, and nobody has ever come back to ask for one.
texte.marktstand-exotic-2x2-west.name: Exotic Food Market Tent W
texte.marktstand-exotic-a.info: Dried pods on strings and cones of spice in every colour. SPICY: enough to cover the taste of anything.
texte.marktstand-exotic-a.name: Exotic Food Stall B
texte.marktstand-exotic-b.info: Jars of the unexplained and a pot of black soup. The board just says ????. So does the stomach.
texte.marktstand-exotic-b.name: Exotic Food Stall C
texte.marktstand-exotic-c.info: A big kettle with a bone sticking out. TODAY, says the board, and nobody dares ask what today is.
texte.marktstand-exotic-c.name: Exotic Food Stall D
texte.marktstand-exotic.info: A cold grill with skewers of something and cones of spice. YUM?, asks the board. The question is the honest part.
texte.marktstand-exotic.name: Exotic Food Stall
texte.marktstand-food-a.info: Cheese wheels, oil jars and a smell that follows you home. Cheaper by the wheel, cheaper still by the funeral.
texte.marktstand-food-a.name: Market Stall: Food A
texte.marktstand-food-b.info: Honey cakes for the winners, garum for everyone else. The chalk marks are what the gladiators still owe.
texte.marktstand-food-b.name: Market Stall: Food B
texte.marktstand-food-c.info: Fresh meat, says the board, with a question mark. The bone in the stew is the honest part.
texte.marktstand-food-c.name: Market Stall: Food C
texte.marktstand-food.info: Bread, sausages and a pot of stew that has been simmering since the last games. Nobody asks what is in it.
texte.marktstand-food.name: Market Stall: Food
texte.marktstand-household-a.info: Lamps and candles, unlit for safety and for profit. Darkness is free, light costs extra.
texte.marktstand-household-a.name: Market Stall: Household A
texte.marktstand-household-b.info: Writing tablets, soap and a stool. Write your will, wash your hands, sit down before the news.
texte.marktstand-household-b.name: Market Stall: Household B
texte.marktstand-household-c.info: The heap of shards is not for sale. It was already sold, to whoever broke it.
texte.marktstand-household-c.name: Market Stall: Household C
texte.marktstand-household.info: Jugs, plates and pots for a home you will rarely see between bouts. Every crack is a feature.
texte.marktstand-household.name: Market Stall: Household
texte.marktstand-intermediate-a.info: Bricks, roof tiles and lime. Everything you need for a wall, except a reason to stay behind it.
texte.marktstand-intermediate-a.name: Market Stall: Materials A
texte.marktstand-intermediate-b.info: Barrels, empty amphorae, nails and tools. Bring your own bent nails back for half a copper.
texte.marktstand-intermediate-b.name: Market Stall: Materials B
texte.marktstand-intermediate-c.info: Strong rope, pre-knotted for your convenience. The trader swears it is for hanging laundry.
texte.marktstand-intermediate-c.name: Market Stall: Materials C
texte.marktstand-intermediate.info: Planks, iron bars and rope for people who build things that outlast them. Mostly arenas.
texte.marktstand-intermediate.name: Market Stall: Intermediate Goods
texte.marktstand-luxury-a.info: Victor's wreaths and gold bars for those who bet correctly. The losers' wreaths are sold at the other stall.
texte.marktstand-luxury-a.name: Market Stall: Luxury A
texte.marktstand-luxury-b.info: Purple cloth, silver plates and a small chest. Dress like a senator, eat like one, owe like one.
texte.marktstand-luxury-b.name: Market Stall: Luxury B
texte.marktstand-luxury-c.info: GUARDED, says the board. The guard stepped out, his spear did not, and the chest lock is already on the ground.
texte.marktstand-luxury-c.name: Market Stall: Luxury C
texte.marktstand-luxury.info: Gold on a tray, a mirror on a stand and perfume to cover the arena smell. Prices on request, regrets on delivery.
texte.marktstand-luxury.name: Market Stall: Luxury
texte.marktstand-raw-a.info: Salt, sulphur and natron in open sacks. Preserve food, start fires, embalm the unlucky. One-stop shop.
texte.marktstand-raw-a.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials A
texte.marktstand-raw-b.info: Logs, clay and reed bundles. Raw goods for raw people, weighed generously in the seller's favour.
texte.marktstand-raw-b.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials B
texte.marktstand-raw-c.info: A marble block, solid as advertised, apart from the crack. The red handprint was the last bargain.
texte.marktstand-raw-c.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials C
texte.marktstand-raw.info: Ore by the basket and by the heap. The pickaxe is not for sale, the stain on it is not discussed.
texte.marktstand-raw.name: Market Stall: Raw Materials
texte.marktstand-souvenirs-a.info: Little clay helmets in rows, one for every gladiator who ever lost. The shelf keeps getting longer.
texte.marktstand-souvenirs-a.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs A
texte.marktstand-souvenirs-b.info: Wooden swords and tridents for children who want to die young like their heroes. Lamps sold separately.
texte.marktstand-souvenirs-b.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs B
texte.marktstand-souvenirs-c.info: A jar of teeth, labelled REAL. For once the board is not lying.
texte.marktstand-souvenirs-c.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs C
texte.marktstand-souvenirs.info: Bloodied rags on a line, bone dice and bottled sweat of champions. Sweat may be from the trader.
texte.marktstand-souvenirs.name: Market Stall: Souvenirs
texte.marktstand-vice-a.info: Baskets of bacchant berries and bacchant's tears. Sweet on the tongue, sour on the purse, gone by morning.
texte.marktstand-vice-a.name: Market Stall: Vice A
texte.marktstand-vice-b.info: Hydra reeds in bundles and a row of pipes. Breathe deep, cough later, pay now.
texte.marktstand-vice-b.name: Market Stall: Vice B
texte.marktstand-vice-c.info: A barrel of Lethe water with a ladle on a chain. FORGET, says the board, including the price.
texte.marktstand-vice-c.name: Market Stall: Vice C
texte.marktstand-vice.info: Creeper leaves upside down, gorgon dust in bowls and flasks of something clear. The chalk tally is the stall's real ledger.
texte.marktstand-vice.name: Market Stall: Vice
texte.mauer-gang.info: Wide enough for two soldiers, or one soldier and his excuses.
texte.mauer-gang.name: Wall Walk
texte.mauer-halb-li.info: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.
texte.mauer-halb-li.name: Wall Crown Half W
texte.mauer-halb-ob.info: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.
texte.mauer-halb-ob.name: Wall Crown Half N
texte.mauer-halb-re.info: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.
texte.mauer-halb-re.name: Wall Crown Half E
texte.mauer-halb-un.info: Half a wall, so the city looks round. The other half was never paid for.
texte.mauer-halb-un.name: Wall Crown Half S
texte.mauer-halb-wand-a.info: A crack the size of a bribe. The mason swears it is decorative.
texte.mauer-halb-wand-a.name: Slanted Wall A
texte.mauer-halb-wand-b.info: The new stone is where someone was thrown through the old one.
texte.mauer-halb-wand-b.name: Slanted Wall B
texte.mauer-halb-wand-c.info: Same stones, different order. The masons got paid by the layer.
texte.mauer-halb-wand-c.name: Slanted Wall C
texte.mauer-halb-wand-d.info: Built in a hurry the year the barbarians were rumoured. They never came. The wall stayed crooked.
texte.mauer-halb-wand-d.name: Slanted Wall D
texte.mauer-halb-wand.info: The wall turns a corner here. Attackers do too, mostly into the moat.
texte.mauer-halb-wand.name: Slanted Wall
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-li.info: Battlements seen edge-on. Thicker than the city budget, at least.
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-li.name: Slanted Battlements W
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-ob-a.info: One merlon gave up. So did the guard behind it.
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-ob-a.name: Slanted Battlements A
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-ob-b.info: The arrow is a souvenir. The stain is the previous owner of the souvenir.
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-ob-b.name: Slanted Battlements B
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-ob.info: Battlements on a bend, for archers who like a view of the whole crowd.
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-ob.name: Slanted Battlements
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-re.info: Battlements seen edge-on. Thicker than the city budget, at least.
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-re.name: Slanted Battlements E
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-un.info: The back of the battlements. Nobody looks at it except the guards, who look at nothing.
texte.mauer-halb-zinne-un.name: Slanted Battlements Back
texte.mauer-kante-i.info: Built to keep the barbarians out. Mostly keeps the taxpayers in.
texte.mauer-kante-i.name: Town Wall
texte.mauer-kante-j.info: Every stone paid for twice: once by the city, once more into the mayor's villa.
texte.mauer-kante-j.name: Town Wall
texte.mauer-rampe-n.info: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.
texte.mauer-rampe-n.name: Wall Ramp
texte.mauer-rampe-o.info: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.
texte.mauer-rampe-o.name: Wall Ramp
texte.mauer-rampe-s.info: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.
texte.mauer-rampe-s.name: Wall Ramp
texte.mauer-rampe-w.info: Built gentle, so the guards can drag the wounded up and the dead down without tripping. Usually it is the other way round.
texte.mauer-rampe-w.name: Wall Ramp
texte.mauer-zinne-n-a.info: One merlon gave up. So did the guard behind it.
texte.mauer-zinne-n-a.name: Battlements A
texte.mauer-zinne-n-b.info: The arrow is a souvenir. The stain is the previous owner of the souvenir.
texte.mauer-zinne-n-b.name: Battlements B
texte.mauer-zinne-n.info: The gaps are for arrows. The rest is for hiding when the arrows come back.
texte.mauer-zinne-n.name: Battlements

texte.mauer-zinne-w.info: The gaps are for arrows. The rest is for hiding when the arrows come back.
texte.mauer-zinne-w.name: Battlements
texte.mauer-zw-a.info: Most of a wall. The rest went into the magistrate's summer villa.
texte.mauer-zw-a.name: Wall Crown N Flat 3/4
texte.mauer-zw-b.info: A sliver of wall so the city looks round from the sky. The gods were not impressed. The tax collectors were.
texte.mauer-zw-b.name: Wall Crown N Flat 1/4

texte.medicus.info: A small house with a slate roof and the staff of Asclepius over the door. The medicus sews, sets and saws for gold; the cheaper the treatment, the longer the scream.
texte.medicus.name: Medicus
texte.menagerie.info: Pens with a moat and a rail. The rail is for the visitors. The moat is for the lawyers.
texte.menagerie.name: Menagerie
texte.mine-erzhalde-a.info: A basket burst and the ore went everywhere. The basket will be docked from somebody's wages.
texte.mine-erzhalde-a.name: Ore Heap Spilled
texte.mine-erzhalde.info: Broken rock with a rust-red streak of profit. The shovel is shared; so are the blisters.
texte.mine-erzhalde.name: Ore Heap
texte.mine-erzkoerbe.info: Baskets of ore and a carrying yoke. Mules cost money, so the yoke fits a human neck.
texte.mine-erzkoerbe.name: Ore Baskets
texte.mine-grubenholz.info: Timber to hold the mountain up. It holds most days. The other days are why there is so much timber.
texte.mine-grubenholz.name: Pit Props
texte.mine-scheidebank.info: Ore on the left, waste on the right, thumbs somewhere in between. The roof keeps the rain off the ore.
texte.mine-scheidebank.name: Sorting Bench
texte.natur-stumpf-alt.info: Grey, mossy and sprouting mushrooms. It has outlasted two foremen and one forest.
texte.natur-stumpf-alt.name: Old Stump
texte.natur-stumpf-frisch.info: Freshly felled. The chips are still pale and the tree has not yet noticed it is furniture.
texte.natur-stumpf-frisch.name: Fresh Stump
texte.natur-stumpf-kerbe.info: The trunk split upwards and kicked back. The woodcutters call it the barber's chair. Nobody sits in it twice.
texte.natur-stumpf-kerbe.name: Torn Stump
texte.natur-stumpf.info: What is left of a tree after the woodcutter has been by. Give it a few days and it will try again; trees never learn.
texte.natur-stumpf.name: Tree Stump
texte.oelmuehle-hinten-i.info: Oil settles in the tanks, coins settle in the locked chest, chalk marks settle the arguments.
texte.oelmuehle-hinten-i.name: Olive Mill W
texte.oelmuehle-hinten.info: Extra virgin, says the jar. The open sack of sand beside it says nothing at all.
texte.oelmuehle-hinten.name: Olive Mill N
texte.oelmuehle-vorn-i.info: The red on the millstone is not from olives. The miller now counts his fingers every morning.
texte.oelmuehle-vorn-i.name: Olive Mill E
texte.oelmuehle-vorn.info: Two stones crush olives in a stone bowl. The donkey quit; its yoke waits for a volunteer.
texte.oelmuehle-vorn.name: Olive Mill
texte.ort-teil-granary-a.info: One stone is gone and an amphora holds the corner up. The rats have sent their thanks.
texte.ort-teil-granary-a.name: Granary A
texte.ort-teil-granary-b.info: Sacks under the eaves and a jar marked with a red cross. The red cross is not for the rats.
texte.ort-teil-granary-b.name: Granary B
texte.ort-teil-granary.info: A grain store on mushroom stones, because rats cannot climb. The tally says the rats are winning anyway.
texte.ort-teil-granary.name: Granary
texte.ort-teil-lighthouse-a.info: Fire off. The keeper says it saves wood. The wreckers say he has a new business partner.
texte.ort-teil-lighthouse-a.name: Lighthouse A
texte.ort-teil-lighthouse-b.info: A round tower streaked white by gulls. The scratches by the door count ships, not days.
texte.ort-teil-lighthouse-b.name: Lighthouse B
texte.ort-teil-lighthouse.info: A stone tower with a fire on top. Ships that see it in time pay the harbour fee. The others pay the wreckers.
texte.ort-teil-lighthouse.name: Lighthouse
texte.ort-teil-mine-chimney-a.info: One stack fell in. The other two are said to be perfectly safe, by the man who sold them.
texte.ort-teil-mine-chimney-a.name: Smelter Stacks A
texte.ort-teil-mine-chimney-b.info: A single tall stack and two slag heaps. NO REST is painted on the board, as a promise.
texte.ort-teil-mine-chimney-b.name: Smelter Stacks B
texte.ort-teil-mine-chimney.info: Two black stacks over a stone smelter. The slag heap grows faster than the town.
texte.ort-teil-mine-chimney.name: Smelter Stacks
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove-a.info: One tree was felled for debt, one leans on a crutch. The grove has the same lender as the town.
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove-a.name: Olive Grove A
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove-b.info: Oil jars waiting for the tax man. The broken one was an accident, the stain was not.
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove-b.name: Olive Grove B
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove-c.info: A ladder with a missing rung and a fresh mound under the tree. The harvest was excellent this year.
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove-c.name: Olive Grove C
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove.info: Gnarled olive trees in rows behind a dry wall. Older than the owners, and kinder too.
texte.ort-teil-olive-grove.name: Olive Grove
texte.ort-teil-palace-a.info: The statue lost its head in the last riot. A new one is on order, slightly larger.
texte.ort-teil-palace-a.name: Palace A
texte.ort-teil-palace-b.info: The garden is going wild and the fountain runs red on feast days. Nobody asks what with.
texte.ort-teil-palace-b.name: Palace B
texte.ort-teil-palace.info: Marble, columns, a golden statue taller than the door. The ruler lives here. The town only pays for it.
texte.ort-teil-palace.name: Palace
texte.ort-teil-pastures-a.info: A broken rail, some bones and a tuft of wool. The fence was technically working.
texte.ort-teil-pastures-a.name: Pastures A
texte.ort-teil-pastures-b.info: A thatched lean-to for bad weather. The herd stands in the rain anyway; the herder sleeps under it.
texte.ort-teil-pastures-b.name: Pastures B
texte.ort-teil-pastures-c.info: Shearing day leftovers and a ram skull on the gatepost. The skull is the herd boss now.
texte.ort-teil-pastures-c.name: Pastures C
texte.ort-teil-pastures.info: Fenced grazing with a trough, a hay rack and a bell. The tally board says forty out, thirty-nine back.
texte.ort-teil-pastures.name: Pastures
texte.ort-teil-ruins-a.info: Half a house and a sign saying FOR RENT. The landlord is optimistic.
texte.ort-teil-ruins-a.name: Ruins A
texte.ort-teil-ruins-b.info: Fallen columns, charred beams and weeds. Somebody lived well here, until somebody else came.
texte.ort-teil-ruins-b.name: Ruins B
texte.ort-teil-ruins-c.info: A tall broken wall and little else. History is written by the winners; the rest is rubble.
texte.ort-teil-ruins-c.name: Ruins C
texte.ort-teil-ruins.info: Burnt walls of a quarter that shrank. The tax notice on the door frame survived the fire.
texte.ort-teil-ruins.name: Ruins
texte.ort-teil-shipyard-a.info: Keel and ribs only, the skeleton of a ship. Optimists call it a frame, sailors call it a coffin with gaps.
texte.ort-teil-shipyard-a.name: Shipyard A
texte.ort-teil-shipyard-b.info: Nearly finished, with a red stripe and a patched plank. The name is painted where the patch will not show.
texte.ort-teil-shipyard-b.name: Shipyard B
texte.ort-teil-shipyard-c.info: Burnt to the ribs a week before launch. The owner was insured. The owner is also very relaxed.
texte.ort-teil-shipyard-c.name: Shipyard C
texte.ort-teil-shipyard.info: A half-planked hull on the slipway, ribs bare like a feast after the guests. The tally board counts launches and floats separately.
texte.ort-teil-shipyard.name: Shipyard
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-a.info: Another tangle of shacks and sacking. The crate with the sign is for let. It has a view of the other crate.
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-a.name: Slum Quarter A
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-b.info: Thatch on one shack, a barrel on the lane. Locals call this end of the quarter the posh end.
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-b.name: Slum Quarter B
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-c.info: Boards over the big puddle, gaps in every wall. The puddle has lived here longer than anyone.
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-c.name: Slum Quarter C
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-d.info: One shack burnt down last night. The sign says fire sale. Everything left is ash, and the ash is negotiable.
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter-d.name: Slum Quarter D
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter.info: Plank shacks, mud lanes and laundry drying on the roofs. The rent is cheap, the rats pay none.
texte.ort-teil-slum-quarter.name: Slum Quarter
texte.ort-teil-suburbs-a.info: A thatched cottage next to a tiled one. The neighbours have not spoken since the roof went up.
texte.ort-teil-suburbs-a.name: Suburbs A
texte.ort-teil-suburbs-b.info: Turnips, an amphora and a trough. The red cross on the door means the tax man has already been. Twice.
texte.ort-teil-suburbs-b.name: Suburbs B
texte.ort-teil-suburbs-c.info: One cottage stands empty, door boarded and scorched. The note says they moved inside the walls. Nobody believes the note.
texte.ort-teil-suburbs-c.name: Suburbs C
texte.ort-teil-suburbs.info: Whitewashed cottages with gardens outside the walls. Cheaper rent, fresher air, free bandits on weekends.
texte.ort-teil-suburbs.name: Suburbs
texte.ort-teil-theatre-a.info: Broken seats patched with planks. Splinters come free with every ticket, applause costs extra.
texte.ort-teil-theatre-a.name: Theatre A
texte.ort-teil-theatre-b.info: Half the upper rows fell in during a comedy. Critics agree it brought the house down.
texte.ort-teil-theatre-b.name: Theatre B
texte.ort-teil-theatre.info: A half bowl of stone seats facing a wooden stage. The trapdoor is for dramatic exits; some actors take it more literally.
texte.ort-teil-theatre.name: Theatre
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-a.info: Harvest is over. Bare canes, empty rows, and a vintner counting baskets twice.
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-a.name: Vineyards A
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-b.info: Heavy grapes and full baskets. A good year, said everyone who did not carry them.
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-b.name: Vineyards B
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-c.info: Autumn leaves and a cracked amphora. The wine inside was already vinegar; the jar had good taste.
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-c.name: Vineyards C
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-d.info: Trampled vines, red mud and one lost boot. Either a very wild harvest festival or a fight about the borders.
texte.ort-teil-vineyards-d.name: Vineyards D
texte.ort-teil-vineyards.info: Terraced vines, stone walls and a pressing basin stained for good. The skull on the stake keeps crows away and pickers honest.
texte.ort-teil-vineyards.name: Vineyards
texte.ort-teil-watermill-a.info: Moss on the wheel, two paddles missing. It still turns, slower than the debts.
texte.ort-teil-watermill-a.name: Watermill A
texte.ort-teil-watermill-b.info: Whitewashed, tiled and proud. Same stream, same flour, higher prices.
texte.ort-teil-watermill-b.name: Watermill B
texte.ort-teil-watermill-c.info: Something came down the stream and stopped at the wheel. The flour tastes of nothing unusual. Officially.
texte.ort-teil-watermill-c.name: Watermill C
texte.ort-teil-watermill.info: A stone mill on a fast stream. It grinds grain, bark and anything that falls in. The miller swears it is mostly grain.
texte.ort-teil-watermill.name: Watermill
texte.pferch-gatter-nord.info: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.
texte.pferch-gatter-nord.name: Pen Gate N
texte.pferch-gatter-ost.info: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.
texte.pferch-gatter-ost.name: Pen Gate E
texte.pferch-gatter-sued.info: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.
texte.pferch-gatter-sued.name: Pen Gate S
texte.pferch-gatter-west.info: A gate of split wood with an iron ring. Close it behind you, or chase the goats yourself.
texte.pferch-gatter-west.name: Pen Gate W
texte.pferch-zaun-nord-a.info: A leaning post tied up with rope. Holds until somebody leans on it.
texte.pferch-zaun-nord-a.name: Pen Fence Patched N
texte.pferch-zaun-nord-b.info: A broken rail tied with a red rag, a bone hung on the post. Wolves are expected to read the hint.
texte.pferch-zaun-nord-b.name: Pen Fence Broken N
texte.pferch-zaun-nord.info: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.
texte.pferch-zaun-nord.name: Pen Fence N
texte.pferch-zaun-ost-a.info: A leaning post tied up with rope. Holds until somebody leans on it.

texte.pferch-zaun-ost.info: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.

texte.pferch-zaun-west-b.info: A broken rail tied with a red rag, a bone hung on the post. Wolves are expected to read the hint.
texte.pferch-zaun-west-b.name: Pen Fence Broken W
texte.pferch-zaun-west.info: Two rails and a post. It keeps the goats in and the neighbours honest.
texte.pferch-zaun-west.name: Pen Fence W
texte.pflaster-basalt-a.info: Two grooves worn by a thousand carts. The wheels know the way to the arena better than the drivers.
texte.pflaster-basalt-a.name: Basalt Paving (ruts)
texte.pflaster-basalt-b.info: Two grooves worn by a thousand carts. Step into one at night and you will limp to your own funeral.
texte.pflaster-basalt-b.name: Basalt Paving (ruts)
texte.pflaster-basalt-c.info: A mule passed here recently. The street sweepers pass less often.
texte.pflaster-basalt-c.name: Basalt Paving (dung)
texte.pflaster-basalt-d.info: A stone was pried loose and sold. The puddle is free of charge.
texte.pflaster-basalt-d.name: Basalt Paving (pothole)
texte.pflaster-basalt-e.info: One sandal, one dried stain. The other sandal left in a hurry.
texte.pflaster-basalt-e.name: Basalt Paving (sandal)
texte.pflaster-basalt-f.info: Basalt from the quarry. Rumour says the quarry still wants its workers back.
texte.pflaster-basalt-f.name: Basalt Paving
texte.pflaster-basalt-g.info: Polished by bare feet, chariot wheels and the occasional dragged body.
texte.pflaster-basalt-g.name: Basalt Paving
texte.pflaster-basalt.info: Big black stones laid by slaves who were not allowed to walk on them afterwards. The road outlived every one of them.
texte.pflaster-basalt.name: Basalt Paving
texte.pflaster-gasse-a.info: Shards, a cabbage leaf, a bone. Nobody asks whose bone.
texte.pflaster-gasse-a.name: Cobbled Alley (rubbish)
texte.pflaster-gasse-b.info: A puddle that never dries. Do not ask what it is made of.
texte.pflaster-gasse-b.name: Cobbled Alley (puddle)
texte.pflaster-gasse-c.info: The stones ran out before the alley did. A weed took over the job.
texte.pflaster-gasse-c.name: Cobbled Alley (gap)
texte.pflaster-gasse-d.info: A dead rat, feet up. The neighbourhood held a small, hungry vigil.
texte.pflaster-gasse-d.name: Cobbled Alley (rat)
texte.pflaster-gasse-e.info: Cobbles worn smooth by people who could not afford a litter.
texte.pflaster-gasse-e.name: Cobbled Alley
texte.pflaster-gasse-f.info: Every stone wobbles a little. So does everyone who walks here after dark.
texte.pflaster-gasse-f.name: Cobbled Alley
texte.pflaster-gasse.info: Round stones packed into dirt. Good for twisting ankles and hiding small coins.
texte.pflaster-gasse.name: Cobbled Alley
texte.pflaster-marmor-a.info: A crack sealed with cheap filler. Like the republic.
texte.pflaster-marmor-a.name: Forum Marble (mended)
texte.pflaster-marmor-b.info: A donor's name, half chiselled off after his trial. The rest of him was removed elsewhere.
texte.pflaster-marmor-b.name: Forum Marble (inscription)
texte.pflaster-marmor-c.info: Pigeons have their own opinion of the senate and express it daily.
texte.pflaster-marmor-c.name: Forum Marble (pigeons)
texte.pflaster-marmor-d.info: Veined marble from far away, paid for by people who will never stand on it.
texte.pflaster-marmor-d.name: Forum Marble
texte.pflaster-marmor.info: Marble slabs where senators walk. Everyone else walks around them.
texte.pflaster-marmor.name: Forum Marble
texte.pflaster-platz-a.info: Cracked under a fishmonger's cart. The fishmonger was fined; the slab was not fixed.
texte.pflaster-platz-a.name: Market Flagstones (crack)
texte.pflaster-platz-b.info: Children chalked a hopping game. Their parents chalked prices next to it.
texte.pflaster-platz-b.name: Market Flagstones (chalk)
texte.pflaster-platz-c.info: Rotten fruit and cabbage. Breakfast for beggars, ammunition for the arena crowd.
texte.pflaster-platz-c.name: Market Flagstones (scraps)
texte.pflaster-platz-d.info: Flagstones scrubbed once a year, for the festival of the god of hygiene, who is not popular.
texte.pflaster-platz-d.name: Market Flagstones
texte.pflaster-platz.info: Square slabs for square deals. The deals are rarely square.
texte.pflaster-platz.name: Market Flagstones
texte.posten-huette-2-1-nord.info: A stone hut under rotting thatch. Twelve men sleep in shifts, so nobody ever has to see the inside awake.
texte.posten-huette-2-1-nord.name: Outpost Hut 2 1 N

texte.posten-rival-ludus-a.info: A rival school with its own yard, posts and banners. Its graduates are buried neatly by the wall.
texte.posten-rival-ludus-a.name: Rival Ludus A
texte.posten-rival-ludus-b.info: Purple banners, polished wooden swords, one missing. The rival calls it discipline; the graves call it tuition.
texte.posten-rival-ludus-b.name: Rival Ludus B
texte.posten-rival-ludus-c.info: Green banners and fewer posts. They train less and bury more, which saves on wooden swords.
texte.posten-rival-ludus-c.name: Rival Ludus C
texte.posten-rival-ludus-d.info: The gate is smashed and the sand is fresh red. Rival schools settle disputes the traditional way.
texte.posten-rival-ludus-d.name: Rival Ludus D
texte.posten-saltworks-a.info: Shallow pans, a cold boiling pan and white heaps. Salt keeps fish, meat and grudges fresh for years.
texte.posten-saltworks-a.name: Saltworks A
texte.posten-saltworks-b.info: A big new heap and full baskets. The overseer weighs the salt twice and the wages once.
texte.posten-saltworks-b.name: Saltworks B
texte.posten-saltworks-c.info: The boiling pan cracked, the crack is filed under next year. The workers boil on regardless.
texte.posten-saltworks-c.name: Saltworks C
texte.posten-saltworks-d.info: A boot sticks out of the big heap and a shovel stands beside it. Nobody has asked, which is very well preserved.
texte.posten-saltworks-d.name: Saltworks D
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-a.info: A cave, a boat and barrels with the seals scraped off. The sign says fishing only; the fish pay no duty either.
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-a.name: Smugglers' Cove A
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-b.info: The boat lies keel up, the barrels moved deeper in. The tide is the only thing here that gets inspected.
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-b.name: Smugglers' Cove B
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-c.info: Firewood in red and white stripes. Somewhere a toll barrier is missing and nobody here has seen it.
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-c.name: Smugglers' Cove C
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-d.info: The last customs inspector stayed. His bronze badge is still shiny, the rest of him less so.
texte.posten-smugglers-cove-d.name: Smugglers' Cove D
texte.posten-stollen-1-nord.info: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.
texte.posten-stollen-1-nord.name: Mine Adit 1 N
texte.posten-stollen-1-ost.info: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.
texte.posten-stollen-1-ost.name: Mine Adit 1 E
texte.posten-stollen-1-sued.info: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.
texte.posten-stollen-1-sued.name: Mine Adit 1 S
texte.posten-stollen-1-west.info: The tally board counts men going in and men coming out. The two rows have never once agreed.
texte.posten-stollen-1-west.name: Mine Adit 1 W
texte.posten-stollen-2-nord.info: The cap beam cracked last month. It is now held up by a rope, a crooked prop and the foreman's optimism.
texte.posten-stollen-2-nord.name: Mine Adit 2 N
texte.posten-stollen-2-ost.info: The cap beam cracked last month. It is now held up by a rope, a crooked prop and the foreman's optimism.
texte.posten-stollen-2-ost.name: Mine Adit 2 E

texte.posten-stollen-2-west.name: Mine Adit 2 W
texte.posten-toll-station-a.info: A barrier, a toll hut and the lord's shield on the wall. The fee is fixed; the man collecting it is not.
texte.posten-toll-station-a.name: Toll Station A
texte.posten-toll-station-b.info: Barrier up, tally on the wall. Somebody paid, or somebody important pretended to.
texte.posten-toll-station-b.name: Toll Station B
texte.posten-toll-station-c.info: The barrier broke and is tied with rope, the old one is firewood. Taxes, at least, never break.
texte.posten-toll-station-c.name: Toll Station C
texte.posten-toll-station-d.info: An empty iron cage hangs by the hut. It is not for sale, but it is for rent.
texte.posten-toll-station-d.name: Toll Station D
texte.posten-trading-post-a.info: A shed, a scale and two stalls at the crossroads. The scale is honest; the little bronze lump on the beam is not.
texte.posten-trading-post-a.name: Trading Post A
texte.posten-trading-post-b.info: Plank roof, ripe fruit, fresh prices in chalk. The prices ripen faster than the fruit.
texte.posten-trading-post-b.name: Trading Post B
texte.posten-trading-post-c.info: One awning collapsed, the fruit went under a cart. The trader sells the bruised ones as local.
texte.posten-trading-post-c.name: Trading Post C
texte.posten-trading-post-d.info: Chains on the counter, collars on the posts. Everything has a price here, sooner or later everyone.
texte.posten-trading-post-d.name: Trading Post D
texte.posten-zubehoer-bruch-2-ost.info: A sledgehammer, chisels on a stone bench, a basket of iron wedges. The stone is patient; the masons are paid by the block.
texte.posten-zubehoer-bruch-2-ost.name: Hut Gear Bruch 2 E
texte.posten-zubehoer-bruch-2-sued.info: A sledgehammer, chisels on a stone bench, a basket of iron wedges. The stone is patient; the masons are paid by the block.

texte.posten-zubehoer-fischer-2-nord.name: Hut Gear Fischer 2 N
texte.posten-zubehoer-fischer-2-ost.info: A net drying on the wall, two oars and a wicker fish trap. The trap catches fish; the net catches the fisherman's debts.

texte.posten-zubehoer-wasch-3-ost.info: A washing pan, a sieve and a bucket of muddy water. Every flake of gold is counted twice: once by the washer, once by the guard.
texte.posten-zubehoer-wasch-3-ost.name: Hut Gear Wasch 3 E
texte.posten-zubehoer-wasch-3-sued.info: A washing pan, a sieve and a bucket of muddy water. Every flake of gold is counted twice: once by the washer, once by the guard.
texte.posten-zubehoer-wasch-3-sued.name: Hut Gear Wasch 3 S
texte.queue-path-a.info: Footprints, all facing forward. Nobody turns back once they have paid.
texte.queue-path-a.name: Queue Path A
texte.queue-path-b.info: A dropped entry token. Someone will be very upset at the gate.
texte.queue-path-b.name: Queue Path B
texte.queue-path-c.info: A tooth and a stain. The queue got impatient.
texte.queue-path-c.name: Queue Path C
texte.queue-path-j-a.info: Footprints the other way round. Still nobody turning back.
texte.queue-path-j-a.name: Queue Path Across A
texte.queue-path-j.info: The same patient gravel, turned the other way. Queues bend, hope does not.
texte.queue-path-j.name: Queue Path Across
texte.queue-path.info: Packed gravel between worn boards. Waiting is half the fun.
texte.queue-path.name: Queue Path
texte.rebstock-a.info: Leaves turning yellow, grapes ripe. Harvest is near, and so are the thieves.
texte.rebstock-a.name: Vine Row B
texte.rebstock-b.info: A post gave way and the basket went with it. The grapes are now stomped for free.
texte.rebstock-b.name: Vine Row (broken post)
texte.rebstock-j-a.info: Leaves turning yellow, grapes ripe. Harvest is near, and so are the thieves.
texte.rebstock-j-a.name: Vine Row B J
texte.rebstock-j-b.info: A post gave way and the basket went with it. The grapes are now stomped for free.
texte.rebstock-j-b.name: Vine Row (broken post) J
texte.rebstock-j.info: Vines trained on posts and wire, heavy with dark grapes. The grapes are crushed by feet, the workers by the vintner.
texte.rebstock-j.name: Vine Row J
texte.rebstock.info: Vines trained on posts and wire, heavy with dark grapes. The grapes are crushed by feet, the workers by the vintner.
texte.rebstock.name: Vine Row
texte.salz-becken-ernte.info: Salt raked into a heap in the corner, the rake left on the wall. The overseer has already weighed it with his eyes.
texte.salz-becken-ernte.name: Raked Salt Pond
texte.salz-becken-kruste.info: The water has gone and left a white crust. Walk on it barefoot once and you will know why the workers walk on the walls.
texte.salz-becken-kruste.name: Salt Crust Pond
texte.salz-becken-sole.info: Sea water in a mud-walled pond, waiting for the sun. The sun works for free and is still the most reliable worker.
texte.salz-becken-sole.name: Brine Pond
texte.salz-haufen.info: A white cone of salt with rake marks around it. Rain is the only thief the guards cannot flog.
texte.salz-haufen.name: Salt Heap
texte.salz-koerbe.info: Baskets of salt, tied sacks and a tally stick. Soldiers are paid in this stuff; the soldiers would like a word.
texte.salz-koerbe.name: Salt Baskets
texte.salz-pfanne.info: A lead pan on a stone hearth, crusted white. Boil the brine, scrape the salt, cough the lead. Two of three are paid.
texte.salz-pfanne.name: Boiling Pan
texte.schild-closed.info: A plank on a stick: CLOSED. The crowd reads it, sighs, and goes into town to watch a hanging instead.
texte.schild-closed.name: Closed Sign
texte.senat-banner-ohne-i.info: A faction banner: two old banners sewn together by a coalition that agreed on nothing but the needle. Somebody has already voted with a knife.
texte.senat-banner-ohne-i.name: Senate Banner Blank I
texte.senat-banner-ohne.info: A faction banner: two old banners sewn together by a coalition that agreed on nothing but the needle. Somebody has already voted with a knife.
texte.senat-banner-ohne.name: Senate Banner Blank
texte.senat-hinten-i.info: The stain on the steps is old. They scrubbed it once, for the ceremony, then voted that it was not there.
texte.senat-hinten-i.name: Senate W
texte.senat-hinten.info: Behind the senate lie the ballots of the last vote, all of them. The result was announced before they were counted.
texte.senat-hinten.name: Senate N
texte.senat-vorn-i.info: A seat is for sale, a senator sleeps on the steps, and the donations chest by the door is the only thing here that works.
texte.senat-vorn-i.name: Senate E
texte.senat-vorn.info: The senate: fake marble over honest brick. Two letters of SENATVS were stolen in bronze; nobody has voted to replace them.
texte.senat-vorn.name: Senate
texte.slave-market.info: A stage, a block and a pen. Prices on the board, chains on the posts, smiles on the trader.
texte.slave-market.name: Slave Market
texte.stands-wood.info: Four rows of splinters with a view. Cushions sold separately, splinters free.
texte.stands-wood.name: Extra Stands
texte.statthalter-banner-ohne-i.info: An empty banner. The last coat of arms was cut off with the last governor's head; the new one has not paid the embroiderer yet.
texte.statthalter-banner-ohne-i.name: Governor Banner Blank I
texte.statthalter-banner-ohne.info: An empty banner. The last coat of arms was cut off with the last governor's head; the new one has not paid the embroiderer yet.
texte.statthalter-banner-ohne.name: Governor Banner Blank
texte.statthalter-hinten-i.info: Where the province is governed: slowly, expensively, and with a good view of the fish pond.
texte.statthalter-hinten-i.name: Governor's Palace W
texte.statthalter-hinten.info: The back of the governor's palace. Tax files spill from the windows; nobody has ever read one, everybody has paid one.
texte.statthalter-hinten.name: Governor's Palace N
texte.statthalter-vorn-i.info: A courtyard with morays, a peacock and chained tax chests. Complaints go in the box by the door, where spiders file them.
texte.statthalter-vorn-i.name: Governor's Palace E
texte.statthalter-vorn.info: Columns out front, heads on spikes above, a pillory below. The governor rules from the courtyard, reclining.
texte.statthalter-vorn.name: Governor's Palace
texte.steg-deck-i.info: Planks on stilts above the water. Each board has been walked on by a sailor, a fishwife and at least one fool who jumped.
texte.steg-deck-i.name: Wooden Jetty
texte.steg-deck-j.info: Planks on stilts above the water. The gaps are wide enough for a coin and exactly wide enough for a ring.
texte.steg-deck-j.name: Wooden Jetty
texte.steg-rampe-n.info: One step up from the quay. Drunks take it in one stride, the tax collector in three.
texte.steg-rampe-n.name: Jetty Ramp
texte.steg-rampe-o.info: One step up from the quay. Drunks take it in one stride, the tax collector in three.
texte.steg-rampe-o.name: Jetty Ramp

texte.steg-rampe-w.name: Jetty Ramp

texte.tempel-gross-hinten-i.info: The back of a great temple. The pigeons have formed their own priesthood here.
texte.tempel-gross-hinten-i.name: Great Temple Rear I
texte.tempel-gross-hinten.info: The back of a great temple. Even the gods need somewhere to keep the firewood.
texte.tempel-gross-hinten.name: Great Temple Rear
texte.tempel-gross-vorn-i.info: Twenty-two columns, one altar, one pyre. The priests insist the smell is incense.
texte.tempel-gross-vorn-i.name: Great Temple I
texte.tempel-gross-vorn.info: Columns all round, a horned altar and a pyre out front. Big city, big gods, bigger collection box.
texte.tempel-gross-vorn.name: Great Temple
texte.tempel-klein-hinten-i.info: The back of a small temple, where the priests leave by the side door with the takings.
texte.tempel-klein-hinten-i.name: Small Temple Rear I
texte.tempel-klein-hinten.info: The back of a small temple. The pigeons consider it theirs, and the gods have not objected.
texte.tempel-klein-hinten.name: Small Temple Rear
texte.tempel-klein-vorn-i.info: Marble, columns and a blood altar out front. Donations are voluntary and strictly enforced.
texte.tempel-klein-vorn-i.name: Small Temple I
texte.tempel-klein-vorn.info: Marble, columns and a blood altar out front. The gods are said to listen; the priests certainly count.
texte.tempel-klein-vorn.name: Small Temple
texte.theater-hinten-i.info: Proper seats for the rich, cushions for the richer, splinters for everyone else. The masks have seen worse.
texte.theater-hinten-i.name: Theatre W
texte.theater-hinten.info: Seen from the cheap seats: arches, masts and a sail that gave up. The stage blood is real; the actor is on sick leave.
texte.theater-hinten.name: Theatre N
texte.theater-vorn-i.info: The gate leads to culture, the arches to the latrines. Rotten fruit is sold at the door, for critics.
texte.theater-vorn-i.name: Theatre E
texte.theater-vorn.info: Eleven rows of stone, one stage and a sail with more holes than plot. Tonight: a tragedy, performed with real knives for authenticity.
texte.theater-vorn.name: Theatre
texte.tier-reh.info: A roe deer, all eyes and nerves. It grazes, it listens, and it has no idea there is a kitchen in its future.
texte.tier-reh.name: Roe Deer
texte.tor-sturz-i.info: The wall walk crosses here. Guards spit on whoever passes underneath, as tradition demands.
texte.tor-sturz-i.name: Gate Arch

texte.training-yard.name: Training Yard
