texte.turm-eingang-j.name: Tower Guard Door
texte.turm-kante-i.info: Three floors of stairs so a guard can look at nothing from a little higher up.
texte.turm-kante-i.name: Wall Tower
texte.turm-kante-j.info: Three floors of stairs so a guard can look at nothing from a little higher up.
texte.turm-kante-j.name: Wall Tower
texte.turm-scharte-i.info: Narrow enough to stop an arrow, wide enough to drop the night soil on visitors.
texte.turm-scharte-i.name: Arrow Slit
texte.turm-scharte-j.info: Narrow enough to stop an arrow, wide enough to drop the night soil on visitors.
texte.turm-scharte-j.name: Arrow Slit
texte.turm-tuer-i.info: Opens onto the wall walk. Locked from the inside whenever the enemy is outside, and sometimes when he is not.
texte.turm-tuer-i.name: Tower Door
texte.turm-tuer-j.info: Opens onto the wall walk. Locked from the inside whenever the enemy is outside, and sometimes when he is not.
texte.turm-tuer-j.name: Tower Door
texte.ufer-schilf.info: Reed sheaves stood up to dry. In a month they will be a roof; in ten years they will be the reason the roof leaks.
texte.ufer-schilf.name: Reed Stooks
texte.ufer-schilfbuendel.info: Bundles of cut reed, tied twice and stacked. The cutters stand knee-deep for this, and the leeches are not on the payroll.
texte.ufer-schilfbuendel.name: Reed Bundles
texte.ufer-torf.info: Peat turves stacked loosely to dry. Wet peat weighs a ton and burns like an apology; dry peat is worth the wait.
texte.ufer-torf.name: Peat Stacks
texte.ufer-torfkarre.info: A barrow full of turves and a basket for the rest. The bog once gave back a whole man. He was still owed wages.
texte.ufer-torfkarre.name: Peat Barrow
texte.wand-stein.info: A wall of cut stone with moss at its foot. Keeps the weather out and the workforce in.
texte.wand-stein.name: Stone Wall
texte.wand-tor.info: A double gate with bronze bands, wide enough for an ox cart. It opens for deliveries and closes for second thoughts.
texte.wand-tor.name: Gate
texte.wand-tuer.info: A plank door with a bronze handle, wide enough for one man. Carts, oxen and big ideas have to use the gate.
texte.wand-tuer.name: Door
texte.ware-bretter.info: A neat stack of sawn planks. Today a workshop wall, tomorrow perhaps a lid.
texte.ware-bretter.name: Planks
texte.ware-fleisch.info: A fresh haunch on a board. Best not to ask which animal, as long as it was an animal.
texte.ware-fleisch.name: Meat
texte.ware-flour-a.info: An open sack with the scoop still in it. Someone left in a hurry, and only one sandal.
texte.ware-flour-a.name: Flour B
texte.ware-flour-b.info: Three sacks and a red handprint. The miller argued about the weight and lost.
texte.ware-flour-b.name: Flour C
texte.ware-flour.info: Two sacks of flour, one with a gnawed hole. The rat is fed; the gladiators are next.
texte.ware-flour.name: Flour
texte.ware-gold-bars-a.info: An iron-bound crate of gold with a chain and lock. Guarded day and night by whoever is cheapest.
texte.ware-gold-bars-a.name: Gold Bars B
texte.ware-gold-bars-b.info: Loose bars, a chain, a padlock and a little blood. The previous owner signed with his whole hand.
texte.ware-gold-bars-b.name: Gold Bars C
texte.ware-gold-bars.info: A neat stack of bars on a pallet. The top one is bitten: the tax collector checks everything personally.
texte.ware-gold-bars.name: Gold Bars
texte.ware-hay-a.info: A loose heap with a pitchfork stuck in it. The red on the tines is rust. Mostly.
texte.ware-hay-a.name: Hay B
texte.ware-hay-b.info: Two bales, and a sword hilt poking out. Never look for a needle in the arena's haystack.
texte.ware-hay-b.name: Hay C
texte.ware-hay.info: A tied bale of hay with a lost sandal strap. Somebody slept here and did not wake up rested.
texte.ware-hay.name: Hay
texte.ware-hides-a.info: A hide stretched on a lacing frame, scraper waiting below. Patience, salt and a strong stomach.
texte.ware-hides-a.name: Hides B
texte.ware-hides-b.info: Rolled hides tied with twine. They roll better than the previous owners ever did.
texte.ware-hides-b.name: Hides C
texte.ware-hides.info: Three raw hides with the ludus brand. Tagged, counted and no longer attached to anyone.
texte.ware-hides.name: Hides
texte.ware-honey-a.info: A straw skep and a full pot. The bees are out on strike, which is why the beekeeper is still alive.
texte.ware-honey-a.name: Honey B
texte.ware-honey-b.info: A cracked pot bleeding honey, dipper in hand. Sticky floors slow down fleeing slaves nicely.
texte.ware-honey-b.name: Honey C
texte.ware-honey.info: Sealed pots of honey, dripping. Sweet enough to make any arena ration go down.
texte.ware-honey.name: Honey
texte.ware-horses-a.info: Saddle, coiled reins, whip and horseshoes. Everything a charioteer needs except a reason to live.
texte.ware-horses-a.name: Horses B
texte.ware-horses-b.info: A padded collar and horseshoes on a post. Mounts sold separately, return policy: none.
texte.ware-horses-b.name: Horses C
texte.ware-horses.info: Saddle and bridle on a trestle, plus one spare horseshoe. The rest of the horse went to the sausage stand.
texte.ware-horses.name: Horses
texte.ware-leather-a.info: Rolls of leather with a blank price tag. Price on request, origin best not requested.
texte.ware-leather-a.name: Leather B
texte.ware-leather-b.info: A sheet draped over a trestle with the tanner's knife still in the beam. He went for lunch. Probably.
texte.ware-leather-b.name: Leather C
texte.ware-leather.info: Tanned sheets strapped in a stack, sandals on top. One size fits whoever survives.
texte.ware-leather.name: Leather
texte.ware-marble-a.info: Stacked slabs and the foot of a victor's statue. The rest was melted down after his last fight.
texte.ware-marble-a.name: Marble B
texte.ware-marble-b.info: A cracked block with hammer, chisel and a red smear. Quarry accidents are included in the price.
texte.ware-marble-b.name: Marble C
texte.ware-marble.info: A block of quarry marble with chalk tally marks. Each mark is a quarry worker it fell on.
texte.ware-marble.name: Marble
texte.ware-meal-a.info: Three bowls of gruel, one tipped over. Somebody found a tooth in it and it was not his.
texte.ware-meal-a.name: Meal B
texte.ware-meal-b.info: A cauldron of gruel with a bone sticking out. Mutton, the cook swears. On his mother's grave, which he dug himself.
texte.ware-meal-b.name: Meal C
texte.ware-meal.info: A tub of barracks gruel, thick enough that the spoon stands up. So do the complaints.
texte.ware-meal.name: Meal
texte.ware-mutton-a.info: Two legs on a board with a note saying fresh. The note is from three days ago.
texte.ware-mutton-a.name: Mutton B
texte.ware-mutton-b.info: Legs of mutton hanging from hooks and dripping. The rack is borrowed from the punishment yard.
texte.ware-mutton-b.name: Mutton C
texte.ware-mutton.info: A leg of mutton on the chopping block, cleaver in place. Definitely sheep. The cook checked twice.
texte.ware-mutton.name: Mutton
texte.ware-oats-a.info: A wicker basket of oats with a sack behind. Porridge for the brave, porridge for the dead.
texte.ware-oats-a.name: Oats B
texte.ware-oats-b.info: Two tied sacks and a fresh sheaf. Harvested by hand, threshed by whoever lost the bet.
texte.ware-oats-b.name: Oats C
texte.ware-oats.info: An open sack of oats and a spill. Horse food, gladiator food, depending on the budget.
texte.ware-oats.name: Oats
texte.ware-olive-oil-a.info: A tall amphora on a stand, leaking. The puddle is premium grade and very slippery.
texte.ware-olive-oil-a.name: Olive Oil B
texte.ware-olive-oil-b.info: Jugs and a tipped flask. Spilled oil is a tragedy; spilled gladiator is a Tuesday.
texte.ware-olive-oil-b.name: Olive Oil C
texte.ware-olive-oil.info: Two amphorae of oil, one seeping. Rubbed on fighters, lamps and the floor where the losers slip.
texte.ware-olive-oil.name: Olive Oil
texte.ware-stamm.info: Three trimmed logs, stacked. Heavy, splintery and always needed somewhere uphill.
texte.ware-stamm.name: Logs
texte.ware-water.info: A bucket of river water, clear enough if you ignore the rat. The rat stopped complaining days ago.
texte.ware-water.name: Water
texte.wasch-rinne.info: A sloping trough with riffles that catch the heavy grains. Gold sinks, sand runs off, hope does both.
texte.wasch-rinne.name: Gold Sluice
texte.wasch-sand.info: Washed gravel, stacked pans and a chest chained to a stake. The chain is for the gold, the stake is for the washers.
texte.wasch-sand.name: Washed Gravel
texte.weg-corduroy-a.info: One log is missing. Something in the hole has been chewing on whatever fell in.
texte.weg-corduroy-a.name: Corduroy Road (Missing Log)
texte.weg-corduroy-b.info: Two logs have rotted soft. The moss is holding the road together now.
texte.weg-corduroy-b.name: Corduroy Road (Rotten Logs)
texte.weg-corduroy-c.info: Someone carved tally marks into a log. Either days on the road or days until payment.
texte.weg-corduroy-c.name: Corduroy Road (Tally Marks)
texte.weg-corduroy-d.info: A red rag tied to a log marks the spot. Nobody remembers what happened there; everybody walks faster.
texte.weg-corduroy-d.name: Corduroy Road (Red Rag)
texte.weg-corduroy-j-a.info: One log is missing. Something in the hole has been chewing on whatever fell in. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-corduroy-j-a.name: Corduroy Road (Missing Log) NE
texte.weg-corduroy-j-b.info: Two logs have rotted soft. The moss is holding the road together now. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-corduroy-j-b.name: Corduroy Road (Rotten Logs) NE
texte.weg-corduroy-j-c.info: Someone carved tally marks into a log. Either days on the road or days until payment. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-corduroy-j-c.name: Corduroy Road (Tally Marks) NE
texte.weg-corduroy-j-d.info: A red rag tied to a log marks the spot. Nobody remembers what happened there; everybody walks faster. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-corduroy-j-d.name: Corduroy Road (Red Rag) NE
texte.weg-corduroy-j.info: Logs laid across the mud so the forest swallows travellers more slowly. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-corduroy-j.name: Corduroy Road NE
texte.weg-corduroy.info: Logs laid across the mud so the forest swallows travellers more slowly.
texte.weg-corduroy.name: Corduroy Road
texte.weg-ferry-a.info: The ferry rope across open water. Hold on to it if the raft is elsewhere.
texte.weg-ferry-a.name: Ferry (Rope)
texte.weg-ferry-b.info: The ferry rope across open water. It is older than the ferryman and in better shape.
texte.weg-ferry-b.name: Ferry (Old Rope)
texte.weg-ferry-c.info: A red rag on the rope and a barrel drifting past. The last passenger argued about the fare.
texte.weg-ferry-c.name: Ferry (Rag and Barrel)
texte.weg-ferry-hut.info: Ring the bell, wait for the ferryman, pay him to cross. Paying him to come back is a separate fee.
texte.weg-ferry-hut.name: Ferry Hut
texte.weg-ferry-j-a.info: The ferry rope across open water. Hold on to it if the raft is elsewhere. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ferry-j-a.name: Ferry (Rope) NE
texte.weg-ferry-j-b.info: The ferry rope across open water. It is older than the ferryman and in better shape. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ferry-j-b.name: Ferry (Old Rope) NE
texte.weg-ferry-j-c.info: A red rag on the rope and a barrel drifting past. The last passenger argued about the fare. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ferry-j-c.name: Ferry (Rag and Barrel) NE
texte.weg-ferry-j.info: A raft on a rope across the river. The ferryman pulls; the passengers pay; the river decides. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ferry-j.name: Ferry NE
texte.weg-ferry.info: A raft on a rope across the river. The ferryman pulls; the passengers pay; the river decides.
texte.weg-ferry.name: Ferry
texte.weg-ford-a.info: One stepping stone is missing. Travellers discover this one at a time.
texte.weg-ford-a.name: Ford (Missing Stone)
texte.weg-ford-b.info: The stones are green with slime. The river collects a toll in twisted ankles.
texte.weg-ford-b.name: Ford (Slimy Stones)
texte.weg-ford-c.info: A wagon wheel rusts in the shallows. The wagon did not make it across either.
texte.weg-ford-c.name: Ford (Sunken Wheel)
texte.weg-ford-j-a.info: One stepping stone is missing. Travellers discover this one at a time. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ford-j-a.name: Ford (Missing Stone) NE
texte.weg-ford-j-b.info: The stones are green with slime. The river collects a toll in twisted ankles. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ford-j-b.name: Ford (Slimy Stones) NE
texte.weg-ford-j-c.info: A wagon wheel rusts in the shallows. The wagon did not make it across either. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ford-j-c.name: Ford (Sunken Wheel) NE
texte.weg-ford-j.info: Shallow water over gravel with stepping stones. Wet feet are free; dry feet cost a stone. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-ford-j.name: Ford NE
texte.weg-ford.info: Shallow water over gravel with stepping stones. Wet feet are free; dry feet cost a stone.
texte.weg-ford.name: Ford
texte.weg-milestone-a.info: Seven miles, give or take. The moss has been counting longer than the empire.
texte.weg-milestone-a.name: Mossy Milestone
texte.weg-milestone-b.info: A carter knocked the corner off. He was fined for shortening a public mile.
texte.weg-milestone-b.name: Chipped Milestone
texte.weg-milestone-c.info: Someone has crossed out the distance and painted LIE. Every traveller agrees.
texte.weg-milestone-c.name: Milestone That Lies
texte.weg-milestone.info: Twelve miles to the arena. The stone does not say whether you arrive as a spectator or as the programme.
texte.weg-milestone.name: Milestone
texte.weg-plank-walk-a.info: A plank is missing. The swamp took it, and the man standing on it.
texte.weg-plank-walk-a.name: Plank Walk (Missing Plank)
texte.weg-plank-walk-b.info: A fresh plank nailed in. The builder charged for a whole bridge.
texte.weg-plank-walk-b.name: Plank Walk (Patched Plank)
texte.weg-plank-walk-c.info: A single sandal stuck in the mud beside the boards. Its owner went on barefoot, briefly.
texte.weg-plank-walk-c.name: Plank Walk (Lost Sandal)
texte.weg-plank-walk-d.info: A broken plank sags into the water. The toll for this section was not reduced.
texte.weg-plank-walk-d.name: Plank Walk (Broken Plank)
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-a.info: A plank is missing. The swamp took it, and the man standing on it. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-a.name: Plank Walk (Missing Plank) NE
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-b.info: A fresh plank nailed in. The builder charged for a whole bridge. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-b.name: Plank Walk (Patched Plank) NE
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-c.info: A single sandal stuck in the mud beside the boards. Its owner went on barefoot, briefly. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-c.name: Plank Walk (Lost Sandal) NE
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-d.info: A broken plank sags into the water. The toll for this section was not reduced. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-plank-walk-j-d.name: Plank Walk (Broken Plank) NE
texte.weg-plank-walk-j.info: Planks on stilts across the swamp. Keep to the boards; the swamp keeps everything else. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-plank-walk-j.name: Plank Walk NE
texte.weg-plank-walk.info: Planks on stilts across the swamp. Keep to the boards; the swamp keeps everything else.
texte.weg-plank-walk.name: Plank Walk
texte.weg-roadside-ruin-a.info: Two walls and a window with no house to look out of.
texte.weg-roadside-ruin-a.name: Ruined Corner
texte.weg-roadside-ruin-b.info: A skull in a niche and a red hand on the wall. Locals call it a shrine; tax collectors call it a warning.
texte.weg-roadside-ruin-b.name: Ruin with Niche
texte.weg-roadside-ruin.info: Once a shrine, then a stable, now a wall. The ivy is the only tenant who pays no rent.
texte.weg-roadside-ruin.name: Roadside Ruin
texte.weg-roadside-tomb-a.info: A family vault with grass on top. The family is inside, the goats are on top.
texte.weg-roadside-tomb-a.name: Round Roadside Tomb
texte.weg-roadside-tomb-b.info: The lid has slipped. Whatever was valuable has slipped out too.
texte.weg-roadside-tomb-b.name: Roadside Sarcophagus
texte.weg-roadside-tomb-c.info: A bronze helmet above the word WON. He won every fight but the last; the broken sword in front is from that one.
texte.weg-roadside-tomb-c.name: Tomb of a Champion
texte.weg-roadside-tomb.info: Here lies a citizen who died in debt. The debt was passed on; the tomb was not paid for either.
texte.weg-roadside-tomb.name: Roadside Tomb
texte.weg-roadside-well-a.info: The well dried up. The owner still collects the fee for the view.
texte.weg-roadside-well-a.name: Dry Roadside Well
texte.weg-roadside-well-b.info: PAY, says the sign, in red. The skull in the trough did not.
texte.weg-roadside-well-b.name: Well with Skull in Trough
texte.weg-roadside-well.info: Cool water for weary caravans. The sign says PAY; the bucket says nothing until paid.
texte.weg-roadside-well.name: Roadside Well
texte.weg-sand-drift-a.info: Deep drifts nearly bury the road. The caravan guide charges extra for remembering where it was.
texte.weg-sand-drift-a.name: Sand Drift (Deep Drift)
texte.weg-sand-drift-b.info: The wind has combed the sand into ripples. Pretty, until you have walked on them for a week.
texte.weg-sand-drift-b.name: Sand Drift (Ripples)
texte.weg-sand-drift-c.info: A skull half buried in the drift: a traveller who thought the water seller was too expensive.
texte.weg-sand-drift-c.name: Sand Drift (Skull)
texte.weg-sand-drift-d.info: A half-buried amphora. Empty, of course; the desert drinks first.
texte.weg-sand-drift-d.name: Sand Drift (Amphora)
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-a.info: Deep drifts nearly bury the road. The caravan guide charges extra for remembering where it was. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-a.name: Sand Drift (Deep Drift) NE
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-b.info: The wind has combed the sand into ripples. Pretty, until you have walked on them for a week. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-b.name: Sand Drift (Ripples) NE
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-c.info: A skull half buried in the drift: a traveller who thought the water seller was too expensive. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-c.name: Sand Drift (Skull) NE
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-d.info: A half-buried amphora. Empty, of course; the desert drinks first. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-sand-drift-j-d.name: Sand Drift (Amphora) NE
texte.weg-sand-drift-j.info: Old paving stones under drifting sand. The desert is slowly reclaiming the empire, one slab at a time. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-sand-drift-j.name: Sand Drift NE
texte.weg-sand-drift.info: Old paving stones under drifting sand. The desert is slowly reclaiming the empire, one slab at a time.
texte.weg-sand-drift.name: Sand Drift
texte.weg-signpost-a.info: The board to the slum fell off. The slum did not notice; nobody goes there on purpose.
texte.weg-signpost-a.name: Broken Signpost
texte.weg-signpost-b.info: The skull belonged to the last surveyor. The new one measures very carefully.
texte.weg-signpost-b.name: Signpost with Skull
texte.weg-signpost-c.info: Three arms, three directions, one destination. The magistrate calls it efficient.
texte.weg-signpost-c.name: All Roads Signpost
texte.weg-signpost.info: One arm points to the arena, the other to the tombs. Most travellers end up following both.
texte.weg-signpost.name: Signpost
texte.weg-switchback-a.info: A boulder sits in the road. Officially it is a speed limit.
texte.weg-switchback-a.name: Switchback (Boulder)
texte.weg-switchback-b.info: A gap in the wall patched with planks. The planks are more hope than barrier.
texte.weg-switchback-b.name: Switchback (Patched Wall)
texte.weg-switchback-c.info: Skid marks end at a hole in the wall. Below lies what remains of the cart.
texte.weg-switchback-c.name: Switchback (Broken Wall)
texte.weg-switchback-d.info: A little cairn beside the wall, built for the god of brakes. He rarely answers.
texte.weg-switchback-d.name: Switchback (Cairn)
texte.weg-switchback-j-a.info: A boulder sits in the road. Officially it is a speed limit. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-switchback-j-a.name: Switchback (Boulder) NE
texte.weg-switchback-j-b.info: A gap in the wall patched with planks. The planks are more hope than barrier. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-switchback-j-b.name: Switchback (Patched Wall) NE
texte.weg-switchback-j-c.info: Skid marks end at a hole in the wall. Below lies what remains of the cart. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-switchback-j-c.name: Switchback (Broken Wall) NE
texte.weg-switchback-j-d.info: A little cairn beside the wall, built for the god of brakes. He rarely answers. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-switchback-j-d.name: Switchback (Cairn) NE
texte.weg-switchback-j.info: A mountain road with a dry-stone wall on the drop side. The wall is for the carts; the drop is for the rest. Runs north-east.
texte.weg-switchback-j.name: Switchback NE
texte.weg-switchback.info: A mountain road with a dry-stone wall on the drop side. The wall is for the carts; the drop is for the rest.
texte.weg-switchback.name: Switchback
texte.weg-toll-barrier-a.info: Raised for the paying. The poor may duck underneath, which costs extra.
texte.weg-toll-barrier-a.name: Open Toll Barrier
texte.weg-toll-barrier-b.info: The tariff reads TOLL: ALL. It is the only honest sign in the province.
texte.weg-toll-barrier-b.name: Toll Barrier with Tariff
texte.weg-toll-barrier.info: The bitten gold coin on purple belongs to the lord of this road. So does everything that passes.
texte.weg-toll-barrier.name: Toll Barrier
texte.weg-watchtower-a.info: The cage is empty. That is the point of the cage, and also its warning.
texte.weg-watchtower-a.name: Watchtower with Cage
texte.weg-watchtower-b.info: Arrows in the breastwork, a gong for the alarm. Nobody has struck it; it would only attract more arrows.
texte.weg-watchtower-b.name: Watchtower with Gong
texte.weg-watchtower.info: A guard climbs up to look for bandits. The bandits climb up the other side to look for guards.
texte.weg-watchtower.name: Watchtower
texte.weg-way-station-a.info: A better station with a tiled roof. The tiles cost more than the guests are worth.
texte.weg-way-station-a.name: Tiled Way Station
texte.weg-way-station-b.info: The sign promises REST. The coffin by the door suggests how long.
texte.weg-way-station-b.name: Way Station with Coffin
texte.weg-way-station.info: Rest, water and a dry roof. The innkeeper charges for all three and for the word REST.
texte.weg-way-station.name: Way Station
texte.weinpresse-hinten-i.info: The tax collector counts jars in chalk. The tithe jars wear his seal, the rest wear excuses.
texte.weinpresse-hinten-i.name: Winepress W
texte.weinpresse-hinten.info: The press beam broke last harvest. The new one is the old one, a rope and a prayer.
texte.weinpresse-hinten.name: Winepress N
texte.weinpresse-vorn-i.info: One jug of water beside every jar of wine. The sign says FINE, painted fresh over LOCAL.
texte.weinpresse-vorn-i.name: Winepress E
texte.weinpresse-vorn.info: Feet washed, mostly, says the sign. The sandal floating in the vat is part of the bouquet.
texte.weinpresse-vorn.name: Winepress
texte.werk-bank.info: A sturdy bench with an anvil and a hammer. Planks, tools and the occasional fingertip are made here.
texte.werk-bank.name: Workbench
texte.baum-tanne-a.name: Fir B
texte.baum-tanne-a.info: A younger fir with a few dead brown branches. It is learning early what the arena teaches everyone.
texte.baum-tanne-b.name: Fir C (axe)
texte.baum-tanne-b.info: A fir with a snapped crown and an axe still stuck in the trunk. The woodcutter left in a hurry and never came back for it.
texte.baum-tanne-c.name: Fir D (red rag)
texte.baum-tanne-c.info: A fir stripped of its lower branches, a red rag tied to a stub. Someone marked a grave here, or a debt.
texte.baum-pappel-a.name: Poplar B
texte.baum-pappel-a.info: A thinner poplar, leaves rattling in every breeze. The crowd sounds just like it when a gladiator falls.
texte.baum-pappel-b.name: Poplar C (dead top)
texte.baum-pappel-b.info: A poplar whose top died standing. Bare twigs point at the sky like a referee who has seen enough.
texte.baum-pappel-c.name: Poplar D (notice)
texte.baum-pappel-c.info: A poplar with a wanted notice nailed to it and an arrow through the notice. Someone found the man first.
texte.baum-zypresse-a.name: Cypress B (bent)
texte.baum-zypresse-a.info: A cypress with its tip bent by the wind. Even the graveyard trees bow to the emperor's weather.
texte.baum-zypresse-b.name: Cypress C (split)
texte.baum-zypresse-b.info: Lightning split this cypress into two spires. The priests charged for both omens.
texte.baum-zypresse-c.name: Cypress D (grave)
texte.baum-zypresse-c.info: A cypress guarding a small headstone with a wilted wreath. The name has worn off; the debt has not.
texte.baum-lianen-a.name: Liana Tree B (chain)
texte.baum-lianen-a.info: A jungle giant with a rusty chain and an open shackle hanging from a branch. Whoever wore it climbed better than the guards.
texte.baum-lianen-b.name: Liana Tree C (strangler)
texte.baum-lianen-b.info: A strangler fig slowly squeezing its host to death. The arena masters study it for business ideas.
texte.baum-lianen-c.name: Liana Tree D (spear)
texte.baum-lianen-c.info: A broken spear juts from the trunk among red blossoms. The beast hunt missed; the tree took the blow.
texte.baum-mangrove-a.name: Mangrove B
texte.baum-mangrove-a.info: A mangrove on extra stilts over a smaller mud pool. It stands in the water so nothing can sneak up on it.
texte.baum-mangrove-b.name: Mangrove C (net)
texte.baum-mangrove-b.info: A torn fishing net snagged in the roots and a dented bronze helmet in the mud. The fishing was poor, the fight was worse.
texte.baum-mangrove-c.name: Mangrove D (oar)
texte.baum-mangrove-c.info: An oar stuck upright in the mud between the roots. The boat is gone, and so is the rower.
texte.baum-olive-a.name: Olive Tree B (hollow)
texte.baum-olive-a.info: An old olive with a hollow trunk. Smugglers, lovers and debtors have all hidden in it, rarely at the same time.
texte.baum-olive-b.name: Olive Tree C (curses)
texte.baum-olive-b.info: Little lead curse tablets are nailed to this olive. Each one asks the gods to break a rival's legs before the games.
texte.baum-olive-c.name: Olive Tree D (half dead)
texte.baum-olive-c.info: Half of this olive died, a frayed rope still tied to a bare branch. Nobody in the village admits to owning the rope.
texte.baum-kokospalme-a.name: Coconut Palm B
texte.baum-kokospalme-a.info: A palm leaning a little less than its neighbours. It still drops coconuts with the same aim.
texte.baum-kokospalme-b.name: Coconut Palm C (helmet)
texte.baum-kokospalme-b.info: A fallen coconut lies next to a dented bronze helmet. The helmet lost.
texte.baum-kokospalme-c.name: Coconut Palm D (tally)
texte.baum-kokospalme-c.info: A palm with dry brown fronds and a tally scratched into the trunk. Nobody knows what is being counted, only that it keeps rising.
texte.bk-kueste-boden.name: Quay Flagstones
texte.bk-kueste-boden.info: Worn harbour flags, sand in every joint. Scrubbed twice a year, whether it needs it or not.
texte.bk-kueste-boden-a.name: Quay Flagstones A
texte.bk-kueste-boden-a.info: Shells, pebbles and a blob of tar. The sea leaves gifts; nobody asked for them.
texte.bk-kueste-boden-b.name: Quay Flagstones B
texte.bk-kueste-boden-b.info: A mismatched sandstone slab, borrowed from a grave nobody visits anymore.
texte.bk-kueste-boden-c.name: Quay Flagstones C
texte.bk-kueste-boden-c.info: A puddle that never dries. Locals call it the harbour master's bath.
texte.bk-kueste-boden-d.name: Quay Flagstones D
texte.bk-kueste-boden-d.info: A coil of rope and a rusty hook. Ask no questions about the last thing it held.
texte.bk-kueste-boden-e.name: Quay Flagstones E
texte.bk-kueste-boden-e.info: A bloodstain and a neat set of fishbones. The fishmonger and his customer disagreed on the price.
texte.bk-kueste-boden-f.name: Quay Flagstones F
texte.bk-kueste-boden-f.info: A broken slab with weed growing through. The town council has been meaning to fix it for forty years.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-c.name: Fishhouse Wall C
texte.bk-kueste-wand-c.info: An empty lobster pot and a coil of rope. Whatever lived in the pot is in somebody's stew.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-e.name: Fishhouse Wall E
texte.bk-kueste-wand-e.info: Salt crust, green slime and a notice with a red cross. The family moved out; the debt stayed.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-f.name: Fishhouse Wall F
texte.bk-kueste-wand-f.info: A harpoon stuck in the boards, still dripping. The argument about the catch is over.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-c.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall C
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-c.info: Rope and cork floats hung up to dry, out of reach of thieves and children.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-e.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall E
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-e.info: White streaks from the gulls. They aim, everybody says so.
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-f.name: Fishhouse Upper Wall F
texte.bk-kueste-wand-oben-f.info: A loose board nailed back on crooked. Good enough until the next storm.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-c.name: Fishhouse Window C
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-c.info: Cork floats strung under the sill, crusted with salt. A window with a view of other people's luck.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-e.name: Fishhouse Window E
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-e.info: Nailed shut with two planks. The tenant left by sea, owing rent.
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-f.name: Fishhouse Window F
texte.bk-kueste-fenster-f.info: Boarded up and marked with a red cross. Fever, debt or both; nobody knocks to ask.
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-b.name: Fishhouse Door B
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-b.info: A rusty knocker and a tar bucket by the step. Mind the bucket, it bites.
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-c.name: Fishhouse Door C
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-c.info: Chalk tallies beside the frame and an oar against the wall. Each mark is a debt or a funeral.
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-d.name: Fishhouse Door D
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-d.info: A red handprint on the planks. Somebody wanted in very badly, once.
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-e.name: Fishhouse Door E
texte.bk-kueste-tuer-e.info: A heap of net and a basket blocking the step. Visitors are welcome to climb.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-a.name: Fishhouse Gable A
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-a.info: Gable boards spattered by gulls. A badge of honour on this coast.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-b.name: Fishhouse Gable B
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-b.info: Moss in the cracks of the gable boards. It is the only thing growing in this house.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-c.name: Fishhouse Gable C
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-c.info: A board missing from the gable. The draught keeps the attic smelling of fish, not of the dead.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-f.name: Fishhouse Gable F
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-f.info: Frayed rope ends caught on the gable nails. Nobody remembers what they held up.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-a.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (down) A
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-a.info: Slates crusted white by gulls, edges ragged. The gulls own the roof; the family rents.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-b.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (down) B
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-b.info: Mossy slates, one slipped, one missing. Rain gets in, so do the rumours.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-c.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (down) C
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-c.info: A gap where a slate blew away. It was last seen at sea, like the owner.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-f.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (down) F
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-ab-f.info: Lichen on uneven slates and a scrap of tarred rope. Held together by habit.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf-a.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (up) A
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf-a.info: Gull-whitened slates with ragged ends. The roof sings in the wind, badly.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf-b.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (up) B
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf-b.info: Moss on the rising verge, a slate askew. Fixed with the same nail three times.
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf-f.name: Fishhouse Gable Peak (up) F
texte.bk-kueste-giebel-auf-f.info: Lichen and a frayed rope end on the verge. The rope used to hold a sign. Then a man.
texte.boden-macchia.name: Dry Scrub
texte.boden-macchia.info: Thin grass, thyme and red dust. The ground here grows olives, goats and lawsuits.
texte.boden-macchia-a.name: Dry Scrub B
texte.boden-macchia-a.info: Grass baked straw-yellow. Thyme smells lovely, which is the only lovely thing for a mile.
texte.boden-macchia-b.name: Dry Scrub Red Earth
texte.boden-macchia-b.info: Bare red earth. Locals swear it was this colour before the last tax collector visited.
texte.boden-macchia-c.name: Dry Scrub Limestone
texte.boden-macchia-c.info: A flat limestone slab. Perfect for drying figs, sharpening knives or settling disputes.
texte.boden-macchia-d.name: Dry Scrub Old Bones
texte.boden-macchia-d.info: A skull and a rusty spearhead in the grass. The previous tenant left no forwarding address.
texte.boden-macchia-e.name: Dry Scrub Amphora
texte.boden-macchia-e.info: A broken amphora and a red stain. It is wine. Mostly.
texte.boden-macchia-f.name: Dry Scrub Cairn
texte.boden-macchia-f.info: A cairn with a stake and a red rag. Marks a boundary, a grave or a debt, depending on who asks.
texte.busch-macchia.name: Mastic Bush
texte.busch-macchia.info: A dark, glossy mastic bush with red berries. The resin sweetens breath; nothing sweetens the neighbours.
texte.busch-macchia-a.name: Broom Bush
texte.busch-macchia-a.info: Yellow broom in flower. Pretty, poisonous and used to sweep the arena floor afterwards.
texte.busch-macchia-b.name: Rosemary on Stones
texte.busch-macchia-b.info: Rosemary between stones. Good for lamb, funerals and hiding the smell of both.
texte.busch-macchia-c.name: Dead Bush with Helmet
texte.busch-macchia-c.info: A dead bush wearing a dented helmet. Its owner stopped here for shade and never needed it again.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach.name: Adobe Roof
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach.info: Packed mud on palm beams. In summer the family sleeps up here, in winter the scorpions do.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-a.name: Adobe Roof A
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-a.info: Dates and peppers drying on a mat. Half for the family, half for the flies.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-b.name: Adobe Roof B
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-b.info: Water jars on the roof, warmed by the sun to the temperature of soup.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-c.name: Adobe Roof C
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-c.info: A fresh mud patch over a leak. It never rains, but one cannot be too careful.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-d.name: Adobe Roof D
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-d.info: A roof hatch with a ladder. The only way out when the tax collector knocks downstairs.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-e.name: Adobe Roof E
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-e.info: A little cairn with a rag on a stick. Burials in town cost extra, the roof is free.
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-f.name: Adobe Roof F
texte.bk-sandlehm-dach-flach-f.info: Bones bleaching beside a broken jar. Last week's dinner, or last week's guest.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster.name: Adobe Window
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster.info: A small window behind a wooden lattice. Lets in air and lets the neighbours watch you sweat.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-a.name: Adobe Window A
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-a.info: Shutters closed against the sun, the dust and the creditors.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-b.name: Adobe Window B
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-b.info: A rug airing over the sill. It has seen better floors and worse stains.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-c.name: Adobe Window C
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-c.info: Clay pots on the sill. One holds water, one holds poison, and nobody remembers which.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-d.name: Adobe Window D
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-d.info: A bucket on a rope. Up come water and gossip, down go the scraps.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-e.name: Adobe Window E
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-e.info: Broken lattice, torn cloth. Someone left through the window and did not stop to close it.
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-f.name: Adobe Window F
texte.bk-sandlehm-fenster-f.info: A horned skull above the window wards off the evil eye. The landlord still gets in.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer.name: Adobe Door
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer.info: Planks and iron straps. Keeps the sand out and the tax collector guessing.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-a.name: Adobe Door A
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-a.info: A patched curtain instead of a door. Burglars appreciate the honesty.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-b.name: Adobe Door B
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-b.info: Left ajar to let the heat out. The heat refused to leave.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-c.name: Adobe Door C
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-c.info: Strings of knotted rope against the flies. The flies have learned knots.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-d.name: Adobe Door D
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-d.info: A red X on the door. Either the plague or the debt collector. Both come back.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-e.name: Adobe Door E
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-e.info: Bones on a string rattle in the wind. Visitors take the hint.
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-f.name: Adobe Door F
texte.bk-sandlehm-tuer-f.info: A sandal nailed to the door. Its owner left in a hurry, and in pieces.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand.name: Adobe Wall
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand.info: Mud, straw and patience, baked by a sun that hates everyone. Holds up the roof and, now and then, the neighbours.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-a.name: Adobe Wall A
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-a.info: The plaster gave up before the owner did. The bricks underneath look honest enough.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-b.name: Adobe Wall B
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-b.info: Red handprints for luck. The paint is ochre. Mostly.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-c.name: Adobe Wall C
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-c.info: A water jar by the wall, sealed with a curse, because a lid costs extra.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-d.name: Adobe Wall D
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-d.info: Rent, paid in instalments. The landlord keeps count on the wall, and on the tenant.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-e.name: Adobe Wall E
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-e.info: An iron ring with a chain. For tying up camels, guests and debtors.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-f.name: Adobe Wall F
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-f.info: A goat skull keeps evil spirits away. It did nothing for the goat.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben.name: Adobe Upper Wall
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben.info: An upper storey on palm beams. Built tall, because the ground tax is charged per foot.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-a.name: Adobe Upper Wall A
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-a.info: The plaster flaked off up here too. The bricks sweat less than the people.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-b.name: Adobe Upper Wall B
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-b.info: An ochre zigzag frieze. Pretty, cheap and a little crooked, like the owner.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-c.name: Adobe Upper Wall C
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-c.info: A wooden rain spout. It has been waiting nine years for rain.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-d.name: Adobe Upper Wall D
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-d.info: A niche with a household god of clay. He takes every offering and never says thanks.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-e.name: Adobe Upper Wall E
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-e.info: A chain and shackle on an iron ring. Some lodgers are not allowed downstairs.
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-f.name: Adobe Upper Wall F
texte.bk-sandlehm-wand-oben-f.info: Red tally marks: days since the last rain, or since the last escape attempt.
